shows.name: Bold Venture
shows.description: Humphrey Bogart and Lauren Bacall star as Slate Shannon and Sailor Duval in a Caribbean adventure series centered on Shannon's Place in Havana and the charter boat Bold Venture, where smugglers, killers, revolutionaries, and desperate travelers draw them into danger.

shows.name: Dr. Christian
shows.description: Jean Hersholt stars as Dr. Paul Christian, the physician of the small town of River's End, where medical cases, family conflicts, romances, and community problems become warm dramatic stories, many selected through the program's listener-written script contests.

shows.name: Michael Shayne
shows.description: Radio adventures featuring Brett Halliday's private detective Michael Shayne, following the tough investigator through murder, blackmail, disappearances, and other criminal cases across several radio productions.

shows.name: Night Beat
shows.description: Frank Lovejoy stars as Randy Stone, a Chicago Star reporter who walks the city after dark, following stories that move between crime, mystery, and the private lives of people he meets on his night beat.

shows.name: Screen Directors Playhouse
shows.description: An NBC anthology of radio adaptations of major motion pictures, often featuring stars from the films and appearances or introductions by directors associated with the original productions.

episodes.title: Deadly Merchandise

A frightened woman and a poet are murdered at Shannonâ€™s Place, and the trail leads to revolutionaries with a cargo of guns who try to force Slate to transport the weapons and make the deaths look like part of someone elseâ€™s fight.

The hunt reveals that Sam hid the valuable figure beneath cheap plaster and used the womanâ€™s arrival as part of a deception meant to protect it from the people willing to kill for it.

When Sam Meston, the man pressuring them, becomes part of a chain of violence, a gun he entrusted to Slate turns into the key piece of evidence and places Sailor in danger.

episodes.episodeDescription: A worried father hires Slate to bring his daughter Cathy home from the gambling ship Blue Moon. episodes.title: The Tears Of Siva
episodes.episodeDescription: Old friend Joe Bishop asks Slate to hold a package, then dies before he can fully explain the danger surrounding it. episodes.displayTitle: A Half Million Reasons to Find Gary

episodes.episodeDescription: A company hires Slate to locate a missing pilot who was carrying a half-million-dollar payroll. The first wrecked plane they find is not his, and the search moves to an island where the missing man, the money and rival searchers all become part of the same dangerous chase.

episodes.title: The High Price of Treason
episodes.episodeDescription: Sailor faces the threat of being forced out of Havana while Slate is drawn into a scheme involving an attractive woman, planted documents and accusations of espionage. When suspicion begins closing around Slate, he follows the links between the murders and the supposedly innocent honeymooners to expose the frame-up behind the wedding party.

episodes.title: Operation In A Shack (1937-11-07)
episodes.episodeDescription: Dr. Christian leaves Rivers End for a fishing vacation with Swampy and reaches a remote river shack to find young Jimmy unconscious with a ruptured appendix. The nearest hospital is about seventy miles away and Jimmy cannot survive the trip, while the doctor has neither surgical instruments nor proper facilities. Faced with almost certain death if he does nothing, Dr. Christian improvises an operating room in the shack, boiling water and using the knives and materials available to perform the emergency operation. Jimmy survives, and news of the feat brings Dr. Christian unexpected professional attention and the possibility of greater opportunities in the city. He ultimately remains in Rivers End, reminded that the ordinary patients who depend on their country doctor are the work he chose.

episodes.title: Steve Charlotte Story (1937-11-14)
episodes.episodeDescription: After receiving national praise for one of her poems, Charlotte Dixon decides that ordinary life in Rivers End and marriage to dependable Steve are stifling her artistic future. She plans to divorce him and go to the city for a literary career, insisting that she no longer loves the commonplace husband she once chose. Dr. Christian sees that Charlotte is romanticizing freedom, so he recruits sophisticated Barbara Powell to make a convincing show of being interested in Steve. At the town picnic Charlotte's confidence in leaving evaporates as she watches Steve apparently fall for another woman. When she abandons the divorce and demands another chance, Steve carries the charade far enough to make her face what losing him would mean, then admits he loves only Charlotte. Dr. Christian reveals that Barbara's romance with Steve was arranged to give Charlotte something more real than poetry to think about.

episodes.title: Tanzy Story (1937-11-21)
episodes.episodeDescription: Mrs. Tansy has spent years doing everything for a household of grown children and in-laws who love her but take her labor completely for granted. They plan a birthday supper in her honor without noticing that she will still be expected to cook it, clean up and continue waiting on everyone. When Christian sees how thoughtlessly they depend on her, he makes the family believe her heart requires complete rest and orders her to bed. Faced for the first time with cooking, housekeeping and supporting themselves without Mrs. Tansy, the family members are forced into responsibility: the unemployed son-in-law must work, the daughter has to use her business training, and the children learn how much their mother has quietly been doing. Mrs. Tansy improves while the household learns to function around her instead of through her. Christian later admits that she had not actually been ill; putting her to bed was his way of teaching the family what life would be like without her and of making them appreciate her before it was too late.

episodes.title: Susan The Opera Singer (1937-11-28)
episodes.episodeDescription: Local singer Susan believes her great chance has arrived when famous opera star Sigrid Holmquist and impresario Otto Kaufman visit Rivers End. Desperate to be heard, Susan even asks Dr. Christian to keep Holmquist from singing at a charity concert when the star seems to be catching a cold, but he refuses to manufacture an opportunity for her. After Holmquist performs brilliantly, Dr. Christian explains that the star once struggled for years through rejection, poor jobs and relentless study before she was ready. Susan accepts that she still has work to do, and Holmquist warmly invites her to come backstage after the next concert, giving her encouragement without pretending success can be rushed.

episodes.title: Blind Boy Story (1937-12-05)
episodes.episodeDescription: Dr. Christian saves a mysterious man who has taken poison and is determined to try again rather than face the disgrace and consequences waiting for him at home. Instead of turning him over to anyone, the doctor asks for a few more hours and takes him on an early-morning call to a poor farm family. There the man meets fourteen-year-old Robert, blind from birth with congenital cataracts, whose family has sacrificed for years to pay for an operation. Dr. Christian removes Robert's bandages and the boy sees his mother, his dog, his home and the dawn for the first time, declaring the world wonderful. Witnessing that joy gives the despairing man a new perspective. He abandons his plan to die and chooses to return home and face his troubles, while Dr. Christian compares life to a game that can be started again after a loss.

episodes.title: Mother in law Story (1937-12-12)
episodes.episodeDescription: Wilma Parker and Howard Ross have repeatedly tried to marry, but Howard's devotion to his widowed mother keeps interfering. He has already sacrificed a promising job rather than leave Mrs. Ross, and another illness on their wedding day postpones the ceremony for a third time. The town begins to believe Mrs. Ross is deliberately preventing the marriage, and she finally admits to Dr. Christian that she does not want Howard to marry because she fears losing the son around whom she has built her life. Wilma feels humiliated and rejected, while Howard becomes too proud and angry to repair the break. During a heavy snowstorm Howard is working on a utility line when he slips and is seriously injured. With telephone lines down and Howard missing for hours, Wilma and Mrs. Ross are left together for seven agonizing hours, each fearing that the man they both love may die. Their rivalry gives way to honesty: Mrs. Ross admits she was wrong to treat Wilma as someone taking Howard away, and both realize there was room in his life for them both. Howard survives, and after the crisis the wedding finally takes place. Christian later observes that giving the two women time alone to talk accomplished what argument could not.

episodes.displayTitle: Young Fellow Who Stole An Auto (1937-12-19)
episodes.episodeDescription: Danny returns to Rivers End for Christmas pretending to be a wealthy New York success, complete with expensive clothes and a car. When the car is identified as stolen, Dr. Christian learns that Danny had actually been working at a parking lot and, desperate to hide his failure and homesickness, took a customers car for what he intended as a short trip home. Dr. Christians testimony helps the court see the difference between a foolish, frightened mistake and a criminal career, and Danny is acquitted and decides to stay home and rebuild honestly.

episodes.title: Woman Who Runs Dress Store (1937-12-26)
episodes.episodeDescription: Harriet Niles runs a successful dress shop in Rivers End and is raising her young daughter Toby in peace, but Harriet is living under an assumed name. She is actually Doris Fleming, widow of a notorious man who murdered one of her former admirers, was convicted and later died in prison. Dr. Christian helped Doris make a new start so Toby could grow up without carrying her fathers scandal. A self-righteous local man named John discovers the secret and insists that Harriet surrender her daughter, arguing that a child should not be raised by a woman with such a past. He pressures and effectively blackmails her until Harriet prepares to leave town and even considers giving Toby up. Dr. Christian investigates John in return and confronts him with what appears to be an official California report showing that he too served time in prison. Terrified of exposure, John confesses that he did spend five years in San Quentin and admits that bitterness over the woman involved in his own case has driven his crusade against Harriet. The report is actually from the state agriculture department; Dr. Christian needed only Johns confession. Rather than expose him, the doctor offers to help cure his resentment, while Harriet and Toby are allowed to keep their home and life in Rivers End.

episodes.episodeDescription: Henry Harris appears to have been kidnapped, drugged and released after a frightening ordeal, and the town treats him with new respect. Dr. Christian notices that the bottle used for the supposed knockout drops is actually an old prescription bottle he had given Henry months earlier. Confronted with the evidence, Henry admits that he staged the entire kidnapping because he was tired of being dismissed as his wealthy wife’s weak, dependent husband and wanted to prove that he had courage and importance of his own.

episodes.title: Auto Accident (1938-01-09)
episodes.episodeDescription: On a snowy New Year's Eve, newly employed Dave Fenton is struck by a hit-and-run car outside the power plant and left with a dangerous brain concussion. Wealthy Marion Brooks soon admits that her own new coupe skidded at the same curve at about the same time, damaging its rear fender, and that she drove on because she was hurrying to a party. Convinced she may have hit Dave, Marion first looks for a way her money and position can protect her, but Dr. Christian forces her to face what the Fenton family would lose. By the time she decides to confess and help them, police report that another driver, Foster, has surrendered: the parked car at the curve was hit twice, and Marion caused only the earlier collision. The narrow escape leaves her changed even though she was not the hit-and-run driver.

episodes.title: Flood Story (1938-01-16)
episodes.episodeDescription: Senator Conway offers Dr. Christian an important Washington appointment heading a national medical commission, with Judy to accompany him as secretary, and the opportunity is important enough that Christian seriously considers leaving Rivers End. Before he can decide, warm rain breaks an upstream ice jam and the river floods. Christian moves through the stricken area treating injuries and directing care while Judy, Jerry Turner and Senator Conway's son Bill throw themselves into rescue work. Bill's willingness to work beside everyone else changes jealous Jerry's opinion of his romantic rival. More importantly, the emergency makes clear just how completely the town depends on its doctor. Even Bill admits that taking Christian away would cost Rivers End something it cannot replace. Christian turns down Washington and decides that he and Judy will continue doing business at the same old stand, while Jerry and Bill agree to let the best man win where Judy is concerned.

episodes.title: Dog Story (1938-01-23)
episodes.episodeDescription: Ten-year-old Tip finds a stray dog he names Jeff while his parents, Eleanor and Dick, are drifting toward a marital breakup. Eleanor believes Dick is involved with another woman, while Dick admits he has become infatuated and says the marriage is finished. Before the separation can harden, Tip falls through the ice on a pond and survives while Jeff dies in the same crisis. Their sons near loss and the dogs death force Dick and Eleanor to recognize how much they have taken for granted; they reconcile, later take Tip on a second honeymoon trip, and help him begin healing with a new puppy without pretending Jeff can be replaced.

episodes.title: The New Stove (1938-01-30)
episodes.episodeDescription: After Charlie Lane dies, his adult children decide that their seventy-five-year-old mother should give up the modest house where she spent nearly fifty years and move into daughter Ella's modern, comfortable home. They mean well, but their efficiency removes everything that made Mrs. Lane feel useful and at home. She is served breakfast in bed, forbidden to help in the kitchen and surrounded by unfamiliar furniture, while she longs for her old carved bed, familiar kitchen, household work and the ordinary routines of her own place. Christian prescribes daily walks and later discovers that Mrs. Lane has secretly been walking back to the shuttered old house just to sit among the things she misses. The cold, damp visits leave her dangerously ill. Rather than keep treating only the illness, Christian tells the family that they have uprooted her identity along with her furniture. Against conventional caution he moves her back to the little brown house, warms it, restores the familiar surroundings and lets the family understand that independence and usefulness are part of her health. Mrs. Lane revives when she realizes she can stay there for good, and the family completes the homecoming with the kind of kitchen stove she wanted. Christian's cure is not modern comfort but restoring her desire to live in a place that still feels like her own life.

episodes.title: The Man With The Paralyzed Arm (1938-02-06)
episodes.displayTitle: The Man With The Paralyzed Arm (1938-02-06)
episodes.episodeDescription: A drifting young man calling himself Homer Moore arrives in Rivers End with one arm apparently paralyzed and a string of inconsistent stories about his past. His deep knowledge of music finally gives him away: Dr. Christian discovers that Homer is actually a composer and pianist whose career ended after an automobile accident. Homer had spent his life terrified that an injury would someday take away the hand he needed to play, and after the accident that fear became so powerful that he accepted the arm as permanently useless even though Christian can find no physical reason for the paralysis. To break the belief, Christian pretends to spill dangerous acid and cries for a towel. Homer instinctively grabs it with the supposedly useless hand. Christian reveals that the 'acid' was only distilled water and explains that the arm had remained physically sound. Freed from the fear that had trapped him, Homer can move his hand again and realizes he can return to music.

episodes.title: War Story (1938-02-20)
episodes.episodeDescription: While playing checkers in Rivers End, Dr. Christian recalls an experience from his service as a medical officer during the First World War. In a village behind the lines he met a terrified young soldier everyone called Slim, who announced that he would desert rather than move to the front and challenged Christian to shoot him if he tried to leave. Instead of condemning him, Christian admitted that everyone was frightened and got Slim talking about the Indiana farm where he grew up and the farm of his own he dreamed of someday owning beside a river. Christian urged him to hold onto that picture strongly enough to carry him through the fear. Slim returned to his unit, was later brought into Christian's overcrowded dressing station badly wounded, and Christian defied orders limiting treatment in order to operate and give him a chance to live. Christian never learned what became of him. Years later in Rivers End, he is called to a newly purchased farm where a man named Catherwood is gravely ill from an infected cut that was neglected because he and his wife had spent nearly everything securing the farm. Under ether the patient relives the wartime encounter, revealing that he is Slim. Christian recognizes him and again uses the same hard-won dream of a farm by the river as something to fight for. Slim survives. Unable to pay much in cash, he settles the doctor's bill with firewood and eggs, and Christian tells Judy that the farm itself did more to pull the man through than any medicine he gave him.

Under ether the patient relives the wartime encounter, revealing that he is Slim. Christian recognizes him and again uses the same hard-won dream of a farm by the river as something to fight for. Slim survives. Unable to pay much in cash, he settles the doctor's bill with firewood and eggs, and Christian tells Judy that the farm itself did more to pull the man through than any medicine he gave him.

episodes.title: Milk Racket Pt1 (1938-02-27)
episodes.episodeDescription: A series of suspicious highway crashes has been wrecking milk trucks around Rivers End, and the latest collision kills a driver. Witnesses place young Bob Marvin on the truck that caused the fatal wreck, leaving him facing a manslaughter charge even though he says he was not driving and refuses to identify the man who was. Dr. Christian and attorney James Benson Clark discover that Bob's unusually well-paid job with the Farmers' Protective Organization may connect him to a protection racket that has been targeting milk dealers who do not cooperate. Bob is indicted and the case is rushed toward trial. Then a representative of the organization offers Dr. Christian first $20,000 and then $30,000 to leave the state before he can testify. Christian refuses, and the man answers with a direct threat that the doctor will never reach the witness stand, ending the first part with the racket openly moving against him.

episodes.episodeDescription: As Bob Marvin's manslaughter trial approaches, Dr. Christian keeps digging into the Farmers Protective Organization behind a series of deliberately wrecked milk trucks. episodes.episodeDescription: The three-part milk-racket story reaches its conclusion with Dr. Christian kidnapped by the men behind the Farmers Protective Organization so he cannot testify in Bob Marvinâ€™s murder trial. While he is being held in a secluded house, one of the gang, Charles Moran, arrives badly wounded after violence involving a milk truck. Dr. Christian refuses to treat the injury as a simple patch-up and insists that Moran needs hospital care to survive. His captors finally allow him to take the wounded man in, costing Dr. Christian his chance to appear at the trial, but Bob is acquitted anyway when the prosecution cannot prove he was driving the truck connected with the killing. Clark destroys only a copy of Moranâ€™s statement before learning that the original is already with the district attorney. An officer waiting nearby arrests him, ending the racket and vindicating Dr. Christianâ€™s suspicions.

episodes.title: Story Of Prisoners Child (1938-03-20)
episodes.episodeDescription: Seven-year-old Patty Elliott is gravely ill, with her mother dead and her devoted father Walt in prison for an old theft he voluntarily confessed to years after rebuilding his life. Convinced that medicine alone will not save the child, Dr. Christian races to the state capital and refuses to accept the normal timetable for parole, arguing that Walt's return is urgently part of Patty's treatment. After an exhausting overnight fight for his release, Dr. Christian brings Walt home. Patty, whom another doctor believed might not survive the morning, revives almost immediately once her father is beside her.

episodes.title: Story Of Windy The Truth Pills (1938-03-27)
episodes.displayTitle: Story Of Windy The Truth Pills (1938-03-27)
episodes.episodeDescription: Windy Smith's lifelong habit of telling outrageous stories makes him the easy suspect when money disappears from Clem Duke's store. Windy answers the accusation with an even wilder tale about armed gangsters, while Clem insists he must be guilty. Dr. Christian quietly turns the matter around with supposed truth pills that are nothing but sugar. Believing the medicine has forced honesty on him, Clem confesses that he took the money himself, lost it playing poker and blamed Windy because he was afraid to face his wife. Windy, who swallowed the same harmless pill, immediately launches into another impossible bandit story, proving that some habits are stronger than any imaginary cure.

episodes.title: Story Of Harry Monroe A Scarf (1938-04-03)
episodes.displayTitle: Story Of Harry Monroe A Scarf (1938-04-03)
episodes.episodeDescription: Judy's married friend Isabel Taylor feels trapped by quiet domestic life and secretly goes out with former beau Harry Monroe while her husband Kenneth is away. Harry has been drinking and drives his car into a ditch; frightened that he may be badly hurt, Isabel runs home and leaves behind a scarf she had borrowed from Judy. When the scarf is found in Harry's car, local gossip Edna assumes Judy was the woman with him. Judy claims the scarf rather than expose Isabel, even though the story could damage Judy's own reputation. Dr. Christian eventually gets the truth from her and turns the scarf into the solution. During a talk to Edna's club on first aid, he uses it to demonstrate an emergency sling and casually says that he himself left the scarf in Harry's car while treating Harry after the accident. The explanation protects Isabel, clears Judy without betraying her friend, and leaves Edna with no scandal to spread.

episodes.title: Landslide (1938-04-10)
episodes.episodeDescription: A spring storm drives Jerry Turner and Jack Wilson into Echo Caverns, where Jerry crawls into a newly discovered passage just before a rockslide seals the opening behind him. Dr. Christian leads a difficult river rescue through darkness, rough water and motor trouble, but the rescuers discover that the passage has shifted and Jerry is no longer where expected. Dr. Christian enters the cave and finds Jerry, only for another slide to cut them off together. Their escape finally comes through a hidden route known by a reclusive local who has long guarded the caverns secrets, explaining the mysterious lights seen around the cave and bringing the trapped men safely out.

episodes.title: The Dishonest Boy (1938-04-17)
episodes.episodeDescription: Russell Brandt steals his poor report card before his parents can see it and tries to shift suspicion onto Ira Nelson, his father's elderly longtime bookkeeper. The lie becomes dangerous because Mr. Brandt has already been considering dismissing Ira as no longer useful to the business. Dr. Christian questions Russell closely, catches the contradictions in his story and forces him to admit that he took the report card and falsely accused Ira. When Russell finally confesses, Dr. Christian reminds his angry father that honesty and courage are learned rather than automatic, and that Russell's lie did not create the father's willingness to discard a loyal old employee. The boy is held accountable, but his decision to tell the truth becomes the beginning of making things right.

episodes.title: Joe Perino (1938-04-24)
episodes.episodeDescription: Dr. Christian is surprised one evening when Rivers End residents gather to introduce a successful visitor named Joe Perino, a man the doctor knew years earlier in Chicago. The meeting brings back the story of Joe as a delinquent boy arrested with a gang after a jewelry-store robbery. Although a judge is ready to send him to reform school, Dr. Christian argues that Joe has never had a fair chance, assumes responsibility for him and persuades the court to suspend sentence. He then convinces the very jeweler who was robbed to take Joe as an unpaid apprentice, even offering to guarantee any loss himself. The trust works. Joe learns the watch trade, eventually goes into business for himself and becomes successful. Now grown, he has tracked down the doctor who once believed in him and repays that faith on a scale no one expects: he donates $100,000 to build the modern Rivers End hospital Dr. Christian has long dreamed of, asking that it bear the doctors name.

episodes.title: Baby On Doorstep (1938-10-18)
episodes.episodeDescription: An unidentified infant is left on Dr. Christian's doorstep with no note or label. Although several experienced mothers offer to adopt him, the bachelor doctor decides to keep the baby himself until the person with the strongest claim appears, and over the next six months he and Judy become deeply attached to the child. One day Lila Bronson, a woman Dr. Christian knew when she was younger, comes in with a sprained ankle. The doctor notices that her toes overlap in the same distinctive way as the baby's, and when she hears the child and asks to see him her emotional reaction confirms what he suspects. Lila has returned for the son she abandoned. Rather than accuse or shame her, Dr. Christian asks whether she would like to adopt the baby and raise him as her own, quietly restoring mother and child while admitting he knew that if he waited long enough the right person would come back.

episodes.title: Boy Loves Girl (1938-10-25)
episodes.episodeDescription: Teenagers Hazel Miller and Bill are secretly in love and plan to marry when Hazel is eighteen, but their parents regard the relationship as childish and would separate them if they knew. Dr. Christian is aware of the romance and urges the adults to remember their own youth rather than treat the pair with contempt. After a disgruntled former employee exposes the secret, the parents react exactly as Hazel and Bill feared. The two run away to a mountain shack and, convinced they will be forced apart forever, begin talking about dying together like Romeo and Juliet. Hazel impulsively takes a pistol and shoots herself before Bill can stop her. Christian reaches the shack in time and finds that the bullet has only torn her side and the wound is not fatal. The near tragedy finally forces both families to take the young couple seriously. Their parents consent to an engagement, while marriage is postponed until Hazel and Bill are older and ready.

episodes.title: Dr Christian For Mayor (1938-11-01)
episodes.episodeDescription: John Hewitt withdraws from the Rivers End mayoral race and decides that Dr. Christian should replace him, launching a draft movement before the doctor can refuse. The town embraces the idea so enthusiastically that Christian's office becomes campaign headquarters, civic groups demand promises for playgrounds, pensions, sidewalks, fountains and lower taxes, and his medical work is increasingly disrupted. Christian wants no part of politics, but Hewitt's supporters reinterpret every refusal to campaign as proof of his devotion to duty. At the public meeting Christian finally finds a medical way to cure the town of its political fever. He describes the costly demands being made on the next mayor and then makes the voters confront the fact that electing him would also mean giving up the doctor they rely on. The crowd quickly decides it needs Dr. Christian more as a physician than as a politician. Christian gives his support to the practical and experienced Hewitt, while the town names Christian honorary mayor as an expression of affection. He accepts the honorary title happily, having preserved both his practice and his friendship with the community.

episodes.title: Tony Donella (1938-11-08)
episodes.episodeDescription: On a bitter night Dr. Christian answers a call to the cramped home of Tony and Rosa Donello and finds Rosa critically ill from a ruptured appendix. Rosa is terrified of hospitals because her sister died in one, and Tony has promised she will not be taken away. When the doctor insists that surgery offers her only chance, Tony pulls a gun and orders him to operate in the apartment instead. With Judy boiling water and improvising sterile conditions from whatever they can find, Dr. Christian performs the emergency operation there rather than abandon Rosa. She survives and is later recovering safely, while an overwhelmed Tony offers everything he has in gratitude. The doctor refuses a real fee and keeps one of Tony's barber tools as a souvenir.

episodes.title: The Accident (1938-11-15)
episodes.episodeDescription: Dr. Christian attends the twenty-fifth anniversary celebration of admired former governor Charles Van Ness and his wife Carolyn, a couple everyone in Rivers End regards as an ideal marriage. Charlie leaves the party on a winter night and is killed when his car skids on a mountain road. After Christian brings the news home, Carolyn finally admits that the public image was false: she had repeatedly protected Charlie's reputation and hidden how unhappy their marriage really was. Returning to the crash scene, Christian finds that Charlie apparently swerved to avoid Cliff Peters, the town drunk, who is also found dead nearby. Everyone expects Cliff's wife Ellen to feel relieved to be free of him, but she remembers a very different man, a loving husband and father whose kindness the town never saw. The two deaths overturn Rivers End's easy judgments about both marriages and leave Christian reflecting on how little outsiders can truly know about another person's love.

episodes.title: Corner Stone (1938-11-22)
episodes.episodeDescription: Fourteen-year-old Freddie Clemons dreams of becoming an aviator and secretly spends time at the local airfield with pilot Alec Skinner, alarming parents who still treat him like a child. After being punished for a forbidden flight, Freddie runs away in an airplane and crashes, then is ashamed to return home. Dr. Christian helps him understand that growing up means facing mistakes rather than escaping them, telling him that dreams are worth building only when they are given a sound foundation.

episodes.title: The Seeing Eye Pt1 (1938-11-29)
episodes.episodeDescription: An automobile accident leaves accomplished young musician Peg Foster blind, and the pity of her mother and fiance Joe Hardy soon makes her feel helpless and incapable of the life she had planned. Dr. Christian argues that their loving dependence is doing more harm than the blindness itself and persuades Peg to attend the Seeing Eye school in Morristown, New Jersey. When the training becomes difficult and Peg wants to quit, he deliberately challenges her pride until she stays. She returns home independently with her guide dog Mara, able to travel on her own and ready to resume the active life, music and future she feared she had lost.

episodes.title: The Pirate Of Rivers End (1938-12-06)
episodes.episodeDescription: A local historian's new manuscript about Rivers End begins exposing facts that respectable families would rather forget. Mrs. Sherman comes to Dr. Christian because wealthy Oscar Duban has learned that her son Brett was adopted and that Brett's natural father served time in prison. Duban uses the discovery to oppose Brett's engagement to his daughter Elaine, and Mrs. Sherman desperately asks Christian to conceal or falsify the truth. Christian refuses. Elaine, however, already knows Brett was adopted and still intends to marry him; Brett is proud of the parents who chose and raised him. Christian then turns the historian's research on Duban himself and discovers that the Duban fortune traces back to a notorious French pirate whose stolen property became the foundation of the family's standing. Faced with his own ancestry, Duban must admit that a person should not be judged by an ancestor's crimes. He drops his objection and gives Elaine and Brett permission to marry.

episodes.title: The Seeing Eye Pt2 (1938-12-13)
episodes.episodeDescription: Blind pianist Peg Foster, now moving independently with her Seeing Eye dog Mara, begins giving music lessons and hopes to earn a teaching position at the McCary Institute of Music. Founder Dan McCary blocks the appointment solely because Peg is blind and even threatens to withdraw his financial support if the institute hires her. By chance, however, McCary hears Peg play beautifully at a pupil's home without realizing who she is or that she cannot see. After learning the truth, he admits that his assumptions were wrong and reverses his opposition, clearing the way for Peg's appointment. The job proves to Peg that she can support herself rather than be a burden, but she still hesitates over whether a blind woman has the right to marry Joe Hardy. Dr. Christian tells her that love, character and the life she and Joe can build together matter more than her blindness. Peg accepts Joe's proposal, with Mara ready to be part of the wedding.

episodes.title: Danny Gets Married (1938-12-20)
episodes.episodeDescription: At Christmas, Dr. Christian watches nurse Goldie devote herself to Tony, a seriously ill boy in the Center City hospital, while young Dr. Danny Bradford quietly falls in love with her. Tony worries about what will happen to Goldie when he is no longer there for her and decides that Bradford is the man who ought to look after her. The adults hesitate to say openly what they feel, but Tony finally forces the question at the child's Christmas celebration, asking Goldie whether she wants Bradford as her Christmas present. She admits that she does. Dr. Christian later explains that Danny Bradford and Goldie were married the following Christmas Day, with Tony recovering slowly but steadily.

episodes.title: The Glamour Girl (1938-12-27)
episodes.episodeDescription: Faith Denton fears that her husband Don is being drawn back to glamorous Brenda Baldwin, so Dr. Christian advises the quiet wife to remind Don that she can be exciting too. Faith transforms herself into Rivers End's new glamour girl, only to discover that Don dislikes the endless parties and begins seeking peace and sympathy from Brenda instead. The experiment reaches its breaking point when a snow-damaged roof begins collapsing during a children's program: Brenda panics, while Faith calmly plays a march and helps lead the children to safety before being injured herself. Seeing his wife's courage jolts Don back to what he nearly threw away, and Faith's recovery restores their marriage on firmer ground.

episodes.title: The Neediest Case (1939-01-03)
episodes.episodeDescription: When Dr. Christian finds reclusive Ivy Fenner freezing and hungry in an unheated house, he treats her as Rivers End's neediest case and organizes food, fuel, blankets, medical care and small comforts she cannot afford. Ivy remains prickly and suspicious, especially whenever anyone goes near her old mattress. After her sudden death, the reason becomes clear: ten thousand dollars has been hidden inside it, making the supposed pauper a secret miser. At first the money appears destined for the state because she left no known will, until the telephone men produce a note Ivy wrote and had them witness when they installed her phone. It leaves her estate to the only good friend she believed she had, Dr. Paul Christian, giving him the chance to turn her hoarded money toward helping others.

At first the money appears destined for the state because she left no known will, until the telephone men produce a note Ivy wrote and had them witness when they installed her phone. It leaves her estate to the only good friend she believed she had, Dr. Paul Christian, giving him the chance to turn her hoarded money toward helping others.

episodes.title: Guest Of Honor (1939-01-10)
episodes.episodeDescription: Riverâ€™s End prepares an elaborate medical-society dinner for visiting Sir Thomas Beaton, one of the worldâ€™s leading throat specialists, and Dr. Christian is assigned to meet the distinguished guest at the train. A fierce blizzard is already burying the roads, however, and Christian has another concern: Esther Denby, a seriously ill young woman living with her family at an isolated mountain farm. Instead of escorting Sir Thomas to his banquet, Christian persuades the irritated surgeon to carry his instruments and struggle with him through waist-deep snow to the Denby home. Once there, Sir Thomas realizes that Esther needs the very specialized treatment he can provide and performs the operation that may save her life. The two doctors miss the dinner entirely. Afterward, warming themselves over coffee, Sir Thomas admits that the exhausting detour has reminded him of something professional fame had allowed him to forget: a doctorâ€™s first obligation is to the sick person who needs him. He raises his own toast to Dr. Christian, the country doctor who made the celebrated guest of honor remember what it means to practice medicine.

episodes.title: Back To Youth (1939-01-17)
episodes.episodeDescription: Forty-two-year-old Kent Lewis has lost his clothing business, cannot find work and has begun to believe everyone who tells him he is already old and finished. Dr. Christian pairs him with energetic seventy-year-old Grandma Nelson, whose appetite for hiking, exploring and adventure makes Kent feel young again and restores the confidence his business failure destroyed. Grandma's worried grandson Ted accuses the doctor of pushing her too hard, but she insists that age is largely a state of mind. The lesson becomes more complicated when Grandma returns alone to an abandoned house she wants to explore, falls asleep after lighting a fire and must be rescued when the house catches fire. Kent proves he is far from finished by helping save her, while Grandma admits that feeling young does not mean ignoring every physical limit.

episodes.title: Chains (1939-01-24)
episodes.episodeDescription: Widowed Margaret Doyle Martin has spent years giving herself entirely to her grown daughters and grandchildren, who treat her devotion as a permanent obligation. On a train trip she meets widowed mining engineer Richard Bailey, falls in love and accepts his proposal, only to have her daughters shame and pressure her into giving him up. Dr. Christian recognizes that their possessiveness has chained Margaret to a life sentence of service and bluntly tells them that being a good mother does not cancel her right to happiness. Faced with Bailey waiting for her decision, Margaret finally chooses the man she loves; they marry and begin a new life together.

episodes.title: The Music Box (1939-01-31)
episodes.episodeDescription: A wedding song causes elderly Miss Mary Loughkin to faint and finally reveal to Dr. Christian that she is really the once-famous opera singer Madame Lupina. Decades earlier in Moldavia she and Prince Carl fell in love, but public outrage over their romance threatened his throne and she left him, carrying only the music box he had given her. She spent the rest of her life in obscurity at Rivers End, and as she dies she asks Dr. Christian to tell Carl that she kept his music box and never forgot him.

episodes.title: Have A Heart (1939-02-07)
episodes.episodeDescription: Nearly seventy-year-old Will Grannis has spent most of his life sheltered by his devoted sister Hattie because an illness in youth was believed to have left him with a dangerous heart condition. Dr. Christian runs a modern cardiograph and discovers that Will's heart is normal, turning what should be good news into the painful realization that decades of fear and restriction were unnecessary. Will responds not with bitterness but with a late-life revolt, traveling alone to a specialist and then across the country and beyond, spending his savings on the adventures he had always been denied. He eventually returns broke but delighted, telling Dr. Christian he packed more life into that year than many people manage in a lifetime.

episodes.title: Angel Unawarepr Snd At End (1939-02-14)
episodes.episodeDescription: Rivers End's council wants the condemned shanties of Paradise Flats torn down, but Dr. Christian refuses to displace the poor families until the town provides decent replacement homes. Contractor Grimshaw dismisses the residents as worthless, singling out the simple-minded but goodhearted Duke Angel as proof that they do not deserve model cottages. When severe flooding comes, Christian and Judy try to cross the river to warn Mayor Hewitt that the bridge has washed out. Their boat carries them to Duke's flooded shanty, where Duke has remained behind with children rather than abandon his home. A floating log destroys the rowboat, leaving them stranded, and the mayor is still approaching the broken bridge. Duke, an exceptional swimmer whom the town has always underestimated, plunges into the icy, debris-filled flood and swims upstream far enough to stop the mayor's automobile, suffering a head injury in the effort. His courage forces Grimshaw and the town to reconsider their contempt. Paradise Flats is replaced by the model cottages Christian had sought, Duke receives a medal as Rivers End's hero, and even after moving into his new house he remains endearingly himself, asking whether he can build a packing-box shanty in the backyard because it would feel more like home.

episodes.title: Washington Had His Delaware (1939-02-21)
episodes.episodeDescription: Unemployed and embittered Dan Smithers has little use for patriotic speeches until work on a Washingtons Birthday pageant forces him to study the real hardships behind the countrys founding. The history changes his outlook on freedom and responsibility just as he is trying to provide for his wife Marianne and their new baby. By the end, Dan has a job, a renewed sense of purpose, and a son born on Washingtons Birthday whom he hopes to name George.

episodes.title: Puppy Love (1939-02-28)
episodes.episodeDescription: Blind Peggy Foster leaves her seeing-eye dog Mara with Dr. Christian while she is away, just as the doctor is again dealing with bitter recluse Mrs. Jackson. Since her husband's death years earlier, Mrs. Jackson has shut herself off from neighbors and grown openly hostile toward animals, while pets in the neighborhood have repeatedly disappeared or died. Mara gets loose, crosses near Mrs. Jackson's property and is later found desperately ill and barely able to move. Dr. Christian confronts Mrs. Jackson, who admits putting out poisoned meat to keep animals away and shows little concern for the harm she has caused. He forces her to understand that poisoning Mara is not merely hurting a dog but threatening the independence and freedom of the blind young woman who depends on her. Mara survives treatment. Shaken by Christian's words, Mrs. Jackson recognizes how thoroughly grief has turned her against the world, resolves to become a neighbor again, and volunteers to lead a community collection to buy Dr. Christian a dog of his own as a sign of Rivers End's affection.

episodes.title: A Bad Case Of Quarantine (1939-03-07)
episodes.episodeDescription: Nine-year-old Patsy Robinson is recovering from measles just as her older brother Bud is preparing for a school dance with Merrily Hamlin. Bud soon comes down with the measles himself and must stay home, so visiting cousin Lester takes Merrily to the dance in his place. Lester proves such a good dancer that Merrily begins spending more time with him even after Bud recovers, leaving Bud jealous and convinced that the college-age cousin has stolen his girl. Patsy, feeling guilty for having given Bud the measles, quietly takes matters into her own hands when she realizes she is coming down with mumps. She carefully keeps everyone away except Lester, making sure he is the one exposed. Lester is quarantined until just before he is due to leave town, while Bud is sent to stay safely with the Hamlins. With Lester out of competition, Merrily makes clear that she really prefers Bud and plans to attend the basketball dance with him. Christian recognizes exactly what Patsy has done and rewards her protective little-sister plotting with an ice-cream soda.

episodes.title: Little Sweetheart (1939-03-14)
episodes.episodeDescription: Polly Palmer returns to Rivers End and throws herself into raising money for Dr. Christian's children's clinic, rekindling the childhood hero-worship she has felt for him all her life. She breaks her engagement to Lee Morgan and mistakes Dr. Christian's gratitude and affection for romantic love, leaving the embarrassed doctor afraid that correcting her will humiliate her. Lee follows her home but, instead of forcing the issue, helps make the hospital campaign a success. Once the work is finished, Polly recognizes that Dr. Christian is the ideal she has always adored but Lee is the man who truly needs and belongs with her; she chooses Lee and asks Dr. Christian to attend their wedding.

episodes.title: Mr Meeks (1939-03-21)
episodes.episodeDescription: Eleanor Meeks loves her husband Gregory but is embarrassed by his contentment with gardening, seed catalogs and time with their son. She wants the president of the family manufacturing company to become more ambitious and important, so Christian helps draw Gregory back into civic and business responsibilities. The change soon produces a much more serious problem. A government tent contract calls for twelve-ounce canvas, but the Meeks company has delivered eight-ounce material while charging for the heavier grade. Suspicion falls on Gregory, especially because his forceful secretary Doris Handen is the sister of a politically connected man long suspected of graft. Christian uncovers a forged factory order and tricks Doris into admitting that the Handens manipulated the order and used Gregory's inattention as cover; John Hewitt overhears the confession so it cannot simply be denied. At home Eleanor then confronts a second apparent scandal, the rumor that Gregory has spent night after night at Doris's house. Gregory admits the visits, but the explanation is absurdly innocent: Eleanor had forbidden his beloved seed catalogs around their own home, so he went elsewhere to read them. The crisis clears Gregory of both fraud and infidelity and leaves Eleanor facing the comic truth that trying to remake a harmless, contented husband nearly created the very troubles she feared.

episodes.title: Spring In The Air (1939-03-28)
episodes.episodeDescription: With spring putting romance in the air, Judy Price confides to Dr. Christian that she is secretly engaged to young physician Ralph Gardner. Ralph is building his career with financial help from a disapproving uncle and has insisted that nobody know about the engagement until he is established. When he learns Judy has told Christian, he becomes angry, tells her to pretend they have broken up and stops seeing her openly. Judy believes he is working nights as hard as she is so they can marry sooner. Christian finally persuades the exhausted Judy to go out for dinner, where they unexpectedly find Ralph dancing with wealthy Laura Payson. Confronted outside, Ralph makes his choice plain: he intends to marry Laura and resents Judy questioning him. Judy is devastated, but Christian helps her see that losing a man willing to trade loyalty for money and position is not the end of love. He reminds her that, like spring itself, love can come around again.

episodes.title: Home Made Hero (1939-04-04)
episodes.episodeDescription: Harvey Gibbons has postponed marriage to Agnes for years while supporting his widowed sister, her children and his mother, and he fears he cannot compete when Agnes's glamorous former sweetheart Mort Hallworthy returns. Agnes is swept up by Mort's confidence and travels with him on the same flight as Dr. Christian and Judy, but a violent storm strips away the glamour when Mort panics and Agnes sees the difference between swagger and dependable courage. Back in Rivers End, Harvey finds work that will ease his family burden, Agnes realizes whom she truly loves, and Harvey finally insists that they stop delaying and marry at once.

episodes.title: Doctor Doctor Come Quick (1939-04-11)
episodes.episodeDescription: At the dedication of Riverâ€™s Endâ€™s new hospital, the town honors Dr. Christian by recalling one especially hectic day of his work. He first treats teenage Janet Hawker after she shoots herself superficially in a moment of despair over public humiliation at school, then gets her to admit she wanted people to understand how badly she had been hurt rather than truly wanting to die. He next comforts Mrs. Cochran, who believes her husband David has run away with his secretary Joan Summers, while also treating young Spike Morse after the boy is bitten by a dog he had been teasing. A report of a possible shortage at Davidâ€™s bank sends Dr. Christian racing to intercept David and Joan before they reach Chicago. He discovers that they are indeed running away together but that David knows nothing of any missing money. A radio bulletin then announces that cashier Elmer Clark has confessed to embezzling the funds. With the criminal suspicion removed, Dr. Christian persuades David and Joan to return to Riverâ€™s End rather than destroy their families and reputations, even inventing a harmless business-trip explanation for their absence. The dedication ceremony closes by recognizing that this mixture of medicine, counsel and community service is simply a normal day for Dr. Christian.

episodes.title: Once Around The Block (1939-11-01)
episodes.episodeDescription: An evening walk around one Rivers End block reveals three households whose troubles are quietly connected. Kit McKenzie has just had a baby, but her husband George resents the new expenses because they have consumed the savings he hoped to use to buy the cottage they rent from Pete Williams. Pete, meanwhile, cannot emotionally let go of that cottage because it is tied to an old love and has become a shrine to his past; his wife Jennifer believes she can never compete with the memory and plans to leave him. The last stop is the mansion of elderly recluse Cordelia Bingham, whom the town believes to be a miser. Cordelia reveals that she has secretly given almost her entire fortune to charities around the world and has only $25,000 left, which she asks Dr. Christian to leave to one deserving person in Rivers End. Christian chooses the McKenzies' two-week-old baby. The legacy gives the young family the security to complete the purchase of Pete's cottage, removing the old house from Pete's life and giving Pete and Jennifer a chance to restore their marriage. The single walk around the block thus links a newborn child's future, a troubled marriage and the hidden generosity of a woman everyone had misjudged.

episodes.title: Bad Boy (1939-11-08)
episodes.episodeDescription: Fifteen-year-old Ted Gallagher is caught with a gang after a nighttime jewelry-store break-in in which the watchman is shot. The town is ready to write Ted off as a bad boy, but Dr. Christian argues that the neglected youngster has never been given a fair chance. Judge Latimer places Ted on six months' probation under the doctor's supervision instead of sending him to reform school. Ted begins to flourish, showing unexpected skill caring for injured animals and an interest in medicine. Then, just before a birthday party arranged for him, Ted gets into a school fight with Buddy Melrose and Buddy dies. Ted admits striking him but refuses to explain the quarrel. Dr. Christian proves that Buddy had a congenital blood-vessel defect and suffered the fatal rupture before Ted's blow landed, clearing Ted of responsibility. A notebook finally reveals why Ted kept silent: Buddy had written a mocking poem about Dr. Christian, and Ted fought to defend the man who had believed in him.

episodes.title: Corn Gingerbread (1939-11-15)
episodes.episodeDescription: Roy Davis grows jealous when Judy spends much of her time helping visiting author Clayton Grant research a book about Rivers End. Clayton is intelligent and charming, and he eventually tells Dr. Christian that he intends to marry Judy and take her away. The surprise is that his book, Corn and Gingerbread, uses Rivers End as an example of everything he believes is wrong with small-town American life and even proposes replacing familiar local landmarks. Judy rejects both his contempt for the town and his proposal, defending the memories and human ties he cannot measure, while Roy happily reclaims his place beside her.

episodes.title: Prelude To Thanksgiving (1939-11-22)
episodes.episodeDescription: Teenager Katherine Anne 'Tanny' Gardner loves her mother but thinks the adults around her are hopelessly old-fashioned. A self-described tomboy, she is especially close to football star Randy Billings and resents glamorous newcomer Jean West. Randy first sides with Tanny's mother against Tanny riding on Bud Collins's motorcycle, then awkwardly tells Tanny that Jean has maneuvered him into taking her to the Thanksgiving football dance. Hurt and jealous, Tanny defiantly accepts Bud's offer of a motorcycle ride even as Randy tries to forbid it. Just after they start off, a truck skids around the corner and Tanny is badly hurt. She escapes internal injury but suffers heavy bruising and a broken arm. The accident forces Randy to admit that he had taken Tanny for granted and that jealousy and his own careless words pushed her toward Bud. As Tanny recovers, Randy chooses Thanksgiving dinner at her bedside over the dance, gives her his fraternity pin and makes clear that she is the girl he wants. Tanny, suddenly less certain that her mother's advice is obsolete, asks her mother what being in love feels like.

episodes.title: Mad Interlude (1939-12-06)
episodes.episodeDescription: Successful businessman Hector Travis has worked without a real break for thirty years while his partner, wife and children continually add demands for money, possessions and plans. Suddenly he locks himself in his room, talks nonsense and behaves as though he has lost his mind, throwing both family and business into confusion. Dr. Christian eventually explains that Hector is not ill at all: completely worn down and unable to ask for rest any other way, he has been pretending to be crazy so the treadmill will stop. His family finally understands what their expectations have cost him and promises not to drive him that hard again.

Suddenly he locks himself in his room, talks nonsense and behaves as though he has lost his mind, throwing both family and business into confusion. Dr. Christian eventually explains that Hector is not ill at all: completely worn down and unable to ask for rest any other way, he has been pretending to be crazy so the treadmill will stop. His family finally understands what their expectations have cost him and promises not to drive him that hard again.

episodes.title: No Crib For His Bed (1939-12-20)
episodes.episodeDescription: Mary Bartlett is nearly penniless after her husband Ben leaves for Center City to find work soon after their baby's birth and sends only a single message in six weeks. Forced from her room and desperate to find him, Mary leaves the baby safely bundled at the bus station with a note asking someone to care for him while she walks into a Christmas snowstorm. Children from the church pageant discover the baby, while Dr. Christian travels to Center City and finds that Ben has finally secured steady work but was ashamed to write while he remained unemployed. On the return trip they find Mary collapsed in the snow and bring her back to Rivers End. The family is reunited at the Christmas pageant, where Mary discovers her own baby safe in the manger beneath the star of Bethlehem.

episodes.title: Love On A Diet (1939-12-27)
episodes.episodeDescription: Dorothy Corbett breaks down after her daughter Margo, looking at an old photograph, innocently remarks that Dorothy used to be pretty. Dr. Christian discovers that years with domineering, jealous husband Dave have stripped Dorothy of nearly every pleasure and sign of individuality: she no longer goes out, dresses attractively or receives the affection she once knew. Treating the problem as emotional starvation rather than an ordinary illness, he and Margo restore Dorothy's hair, clothes and confidence and arrange harmless masculine attention from Arnold Darrow, who is actually Margo's fiancé. Dave returns unexpectedly, sees his transformed wife with Arnold and assumes an affair, even threatening divorce and blaming Dr. Christian. The doctor forces Dave to confront the truth that his possessiveness has nearly destroyed Dorothy. When Margo reveals Arnold belongs to her, Dorothy's collapse finally breaks through Dave's anger. He calls his wife by the old pet name 'Dolly' and resumes the tenderness he abandoned years earlier, giving her a reason to want life again.

episodes.title: None So Blind (1940-01-03)
episodes.episodeDescription: Twelve-year-old Mary Dugan of Squatterstown is treated as the awkward, troublesome sister beside pretty Lillian and is finally thrown out of Mrs. Mudge's girls' club after another clash. Dr. Christian suspects that Mary's hostility is covering years of humiliation and notices something the adults around her have missed: an exceptional natural ear for music. He introduces Mary to blind pianist Peg Foster. Because Peg cannot judge the child by dirty clothes, looks or social standing, she responds to Mary's voice, personality and musical ability instead. Peg begins teaching her, protects her when Mrs. Mudge tries to shame her, and Mary rapidly develops into a gifted young pianist. After only a few months Mary performs publicly and wins a McCary Institute scholarship. When Mrs. Mudge suggests that some of the scholarship money can be diverted to buy things for Lillian, Christian and Peg make clear that the award belongs to Mary's education. The girl everyone dismissed as the ugly duckling finally has a future built on the talent others were too prejudiced to see.

episodes.title: There Is No Such Thing As Luck (1940-01-10)
episodes.displayTitle: There Is No Such Thing As Luck (1940-01-10)
episodes.sortKey: 0|1940-01-10|00062|there is no such thing as luck 1940 01 10
episodes.episodeDescription: Wealthy fashion heir Henry Martin III comes to Dr. Christian miserable with his pampered business life and convinced that what he really needs is honest work on a farm. Christian pairs him with struggling farmer Tim Halsey and daughter Molly: Martin takes over the Halsey farm while the Halseys live in his Chicago apartment, with Martin also paying them a monthly allowance. The arrangement succeeds so well that Martin turns the farm into a profitable operation and wants to keep it, but after nearly a year the Halseys decide to return. When they refuse an extension, Martin threatens to sue Christian for $100,000 over the doctor's guarantee that he could remain. The dispute collapses when Molly reveals that she has used her time in Chicago to study fashion design. Her self-made clothes immediately impress Martin, who forgets the lawsuit and wants her for his firm. Soon afterward Molly writes that she and Martin plan to marry, leaving Christian amused that luck has solved a problem Martin insisted luck did not exist.

episodes.title: Stuff Of Heroes (1940-01-17)
episodes.episodeDescription: Hospital handyman Hank Blevins has spent years letting his reckless brother Luke bully him and clean up after Luke's gambling debts. When Dr. Christian refuses to supply money for another rescue, Luke pressures Hank into stealing the hospital's valuable radium, arguing that no one will suspect him and that the theft will keep Luke out of jail. Hank gives in, but the theft leaves him miserable, especially after Dr. Christian explains that the radium is medically vital, registered and dangerous to anyone who mishandles it. Hank finally confronts Luke, takes the radium back and returns it to the hospital, earning a black eye in the struggle. Dr. Christian quietly lets the disappearance remain a secret and tells Hank that a man who can stand up for what is right after years of fear has the stuff that heroes are made of.

episodes.title: Revolt (1940-01-24)
episodes.episodeDescription: Nineteen-year-old Bill and Helen arrive in Rivers End posing as brother and sister after running away from Minneapolis. Resentful of what he calls a system that keeps young people powerless, Bill plans to rob Dr. Christian's safe and pressures Helen to learn the combination, eventually threatening the doctor with a gun. Dr. Christian has already recognized their lies, found the police bulletin and quietly removed the cartridges from Bill's weapon. Confronted with how completely his rebellion has turned into crime, Bill abandons the robbery and decides to return voluntarily, face the consequences and then work honestly toward a future. Helen's mother is coming to take her home, and the two young people leave their marriage plans for a more responsible time.

episodes.title: Gypsy Love (1940-01-31)
episodes.episodeDescription: On the eve of his wedding to Maria, gypsy prince Marko collapses with violent weakness that the camp believes is a black spell placed by Sarah, a woman who loves him and has vowed he will marry her or die. Maria secretly summons Dr. Christian despite the band's distrust of outside medicine. He notices that Sarah has been helping nurse Marko and tests the broth she gives him, discovering an obscure drug whose effects have been magnified by Marko's terror of the curse. Dr. Christian and the police stop Sarah before the dosing can become fatal. Marko recovers, Sarah is held until he is out of danger, and Dr. Christian returns to dance at Marko and Maria's wedding.

episodes.title: Stranger Things (1940-02-07)
episodes.episodeDescription: Investment broker Joe Fletcher leaves thirty thousand dollars in bonds with town treasurer Harvey Ziegler, only to learn that Ziegler's safe has apparently been robbed. At the same time Joe's young son Alan suffers vivid recurring dreams containing details that seem to point toward the crime. With no conventional evidence, Dr. Christian uses the dream's clues to confront Ziegler, including a hidden compartment and an arm injury caused by the safe. Ziegler confesses to staging the robbery himself, leaving Dr. Christian unable to explain how Alan knew the truth except to acknowledge that some strange things remain beyond science.

episodes.title: My True Valentine (1940-02-14)
episodes.episodeDescription: In 1925, seamstress Emily Cobb is engaged to Don Burns, a young man with a wild reputation who is trying to straighten out his life. After a machine-works robbery, watchman Joel Sims identifies one of the nearly identical Burns brothers before being shot to death. Don's brother Sandy is known to be away, leaving Don without an alibi, and Don is convicted despite insisting he is innocent. He refuses to let Emily tie her life to his and spends years in prison while she eventually builds a successful fashion business in Chicago. Fifteen years later Emily returns to Rivers End on Valentine's Day, torn over whether to marry a kind, successful man who loves her even though she still loves Don. At the same time Don returns after being cleared when the real killer confesses while already serving a life sentence on another charge. Emily decides before knowing Don is back that she cannot marry anyone else, and Dr. Christian reunites the two, suggesting that after all those lost years Valentine's Day is an appropriate day for their wedding.

episodes.title: Leap No More My Lady (1940-02-28)
episodes.episodeDescription: Librarian Lucy Plum has spent years waiting on self-centered George Kegley, while the shy but dependable Stan Sherwood quietly cares about her. Dr. Christian and Judy push Lucy to stop arranging her life around George and deliberately let an engagement scheme go far enough to force everyone to show what they really want. When George plans an immediate wedding and a move away, Stan finally protests and admits he cannot bear to lose Lucy. Lucy realizes she no longer loves George, and the manufactured crisis clears the way for her and Stan.

episodes.title: Blossom Otoole (1940-03-06)
episodes.episodeDescription: Years after young Claire Barnes ran away when her stern father refused to accept her love for Harry Hall, Dr. Christian learns that the now-elderly Barnes is dying and sends for the daughter he has never stopped missing. Claire returns as Blossom O'Toole, the stage name she adopted after leaving home. She admits to Christian that she and Harry never married and that her hoped-for theatrical success never came; Blossom is only a struggling second-rate actress. She is ashamed to let her father know how little came of the life she chose, but Christian persuades her to see him. At his bedside Claire allows the dying man to believe that she is happy and successful, giving him the comfort and pride he needs in his final moments. The reunion lets father and daughter make peace without forcing Claire to destroy the image that eases his death.

episodes.title: Angies Last Cure (1940-03-13)
episodes.episodeDescription: Angie Hopper becomes an obsessive hypochondriac after buying a popular book of symptoms, diagnosing herself with one illness after another and keeping exhausted husband Fred constantly waiting on her. Dr. Christian sees that arguing with her fears will accomplish nothing. When Fred develops an ordinary ache, Angie immediately transfers all her attention to him, and Dr. Christian quietly encourages the reversal by giving Fred's harmless baldness the impressive name of a chronic glabrous condition. Caring for Fred cures Angie of her own imaginary diseases so completely that she throws the symptom book into the fire.

episodes.title: Spring Dance (1940-03-20)
episodes.episodeDescription: Seventeen-year-old Bunn Williams, captain of the high-school basketball team, feels badly out of his depth at Sally Sans's sophisticated birthday dance. Convinced that wealthier Ken Carson and expensive gifts make his own dinner jacket, flowers and old-fashioned present look foolish, Bunn nearly gives up before telling Sally how he feels. Sally makes clear that the things he thought were embarrassments matter because they came from him, wears his flowers and agrees to be his girl. Their spring evening ends with Bunn wishing on the first star and Dr. Christian observing that his wish seems to have come true.

episodes.title: Visiting Lady (1940-03-27)
episodes.episodeDescription: Rivers End goes overboard entertaining glamorous New York visitor Brenda Marsh, while Judy and the other townspeople exhaust themselves trying to prove how sophisticated the village can be. Brenda finally admits to Dr. Christian that she came to the country hoping to escape exactly this kind of social whirl and simply wants a chance to rest. During a drive, an out-of-control truck causes a serious crash that leaves Judy badly injured; Brenda keeps her head, gets Dr. Christian and Judy to help, and earns the town's respect as far more than an artificial society girl. Judy recovers, Roy's fright makes his feelings for her unmistakable, and Brenda's only remaining request is that Rivers End please stop giving parties for her.

episodes.title: Derelicts (1940-04-03)
episodes.episodeDescription: Police bring alcoholic drifter Jim Martin into the hospital, where Dr. Christian discovers that the watch Jim guards so fiercely is one of the few things left from the life he lost. Jim was once the successful author of the popular Danny Dean children's books, but after an automobile accident killed his wife and son while he was driving, guilt destroyed his family life and his career and he drifted into drink. In the next room, an orphan boy named Les is recovering from pneumonia and happens to adore the Danny Dean stories. Christian brings the two together without initially revealing Jim's identity. Les's admiration draws Jim back into storytelling, and Jim begins writing again. When officials prepare to return Les to an institution, Jim finally recognizes that both of them have been living as derelicts without families. He races to the station, stops the boy from being sent away and announces that he will adopt Les, giving both of them a home and a new start.

episodes.title: Chicken Supreme (1940-04-10)
episodes.episodeDescription: Dr. Christian receives an unwanted hen named Ella as payment from a poor patient and uses the odd gift while trying to help proud sisters Matilda and Lottie Tweedle find a useful occupation and a way to support themselves. At first the sisters intend to turn Ella into dinner, but failed attempts with a hatchet and then a shotgun leave them far too attached to the bird to kill her. Ella soon leads them into raising chicks, and what begins as sentiment becomes a serious poultry project. The women study feeding and breeding, rise early to care for the flock and devote themselves to building it properly. Their birds attract a buyer, and Christian helps them see how the operation can expand into a real business with more stock, runs, equipment and feed. The sisters gain work, independence and purpose. Their gratitude creates one last comic crisis when they decide the finest possible thank-you for Dr. Christian is to give him the best chicken in their flock, freshly killed.

episodes.title: Glamour (1940-04-17)
episodes.episodeDescription: Thirteen years earlier, young widow Ellen McCarty asked Dr. Christian to find a home for her three-year-old daughter Glamour because Ellen intended to marry wealthy Carter Gaylord, who did not know the child existed. John and Evie Clark raised Glamour with Ellen's financial support. After Gaylord's death, Ellen returns to Rivers End and seeks custody of the now sixteen-year-old girl, promising wealth, travel and every social advantage. A judge leaves the final choice to Glamour. When Christian refuses to influence her, Ellen tries to force the decision by offering lifelong security to the Clarks if Glamour comes with her and threatening to withdraw every cent if she refuses. Glamour angrily chooses John and Evie and rejects the mother who abandoned her. The confrontation brings on another heart attack for Evie, and Ellen finally begins to understand that money and pressure cannot manufacture affection. Christian tells her that if she truly wants her daughter back in her life she must earn that relationship through patience and consideration. He suggests that Ellen build a summer cottage nearby, giving mother and daughter a chance to know each other gradually without uprooting Glamour from the family that raised her.

episodes.title: Riders On The Storm (1940-04-24)
episodes.episodeDescription: Former test pilot Jim Waters has been grounded and emotionally shattered by an earlier accident that cost another man his life. With Dr. Christians encouragement he begins working again and builds a new plane, but his real test comes when a medical emergency on a remote island arises during a violent storm. Jim flies Dr. Christian through icing, poor visibility and mechanical trouble, risking his life to reach the patient and discovering that he can honor the life he lost by saving another rather than destroying himself with guilt.

episodes.title: Unfinished Business (1940-05-15)
episodes.episodeDescription: Benjamin Stack has organized every minute of his marriage into a rigid schedule until his wife Maddie finally leaves, saying she has lived with a system instead of a man. Dr. Christian tries to help them reconcile, but even when Maddie asks only for spontaneity, Benjamin immediately tries to turn their life together into a modified timetable. After losing her again, his ordered world collapses so completely that he prepares to jump from a building. Dr. Christian talks him down by appealing to the one thing Benjamin still cannot abandon: an unpaid obligation, inventing a large medical bill that must be settled first. With the immediate crisis over, Dr. Christian recommends an unplanned road trip with Maddie, although Benjamin's first instinct is still to schedule every mile and meal.

episodes.title: Between Office Hours (1940-05-22)
episodes.episodeDescription: Bruiser Burns, a wrestler and convicted killer being taken for psychiatric observation, badly crushes three fingers in a car door. Dr. Christian has no choice but to amputate the mangled fingers to save the arm. Months later Burns is judged criminally insane and escapes while being transferred from the asylum, convinced that Christian deliberately ruined his fighting career. He tracks the doctor to his office during the supposedly quiet gap between office hours and holds Judy while waiting to kill them both. Christian wakes from a nap, realizes the escaped man is inside, darkens the office and helps trip and overpower him. Even after Burns has tried to murder him, Christian notices something lodged in the man's inflamed eye and calmly removes it before the police arrive.

episodes.title: Ten Meter Romance (1940-05-29)
episodes.episodeDescription: Albert Holly becomes lonely and despondent after his daughter Ethel marries and moves to the Philippines. Dr. Christian steers him toward amateur radio, and the ten-meter band gives Albert a new purpose: he can speak with Ethel across the ocean and eventually becomes a regular on-air friend of widowed operator Mrs. Winters. The nightly conversations cure the vague 'heart trouble' Albert had been complaining about and grow into a romance even though the two have never met face to face. When Ethel's family prepares to return closer to home, Albert decides to invite Mrs. Winters to Rivers End and ask her to marry him, with Dr. Christian coaching him to make the proposal as simply over the radio as he would make any other call.

episodes.title: Roughneck (1940-06-05)
episodes.episodeDescription: Jockey Joseph Meadows is badly injured when thrown from his horse Roughneck and is left unable to move his legs. Another doctor expects permanent paralysis, but Dr. Christian believes Meadows may recover if he has a powerful enough reason to fight. Meadows' fourteen-year-old son Jimmy is determined to get Roughneck into the Memorial Stakes, the big race his father had been working toward before the accident. Christian takes Jimmy and the horse under his wing, reins in the boy's attempts to gamble for the entry fee and helps Rivers End raise the money by selling small shares in Roughneck. The approaching race gives Meadows a goal, and his rehabilitation progresses from a specially built walker to crutches. At the Memorial Stakes Jimmy rides Roughneck as the Rivers End entry. Roughneck wins by half a length, and in the excitement Meadows suddenly realizes he has risen to his feet without his crutches. The horse's victory becomes the final push in Meadows' own recovery.

episodes.title: Bensons Inventions (1940-06-12)
episodes.episodeDescription: Buzz Benson is Rivers End's much-ridiculed school janitor and amateur inventor, better known for failed gadgets and pranks than for serious ability. Dr. Christian discovers that Buzz has a genuine interest in chemistry and quietly coaches him. When word spreads that Buzz has invented a revolutionary 'chemical motor' and that Christian plans to send him to New York, townsmen who had mocked Buzz suddenly call him a genius, argue that his discovery belongs in Rivers End and begin maneuvering for a share of the supposed fortune. Their enthusiasm grows into a public meeting built around developing the motor locally. Christian finally exposes the mistake: he never vouched for Buzz's chemical motor at all. The real achievement is a useful precipitation process Buzz discovered accidentally, and Christian has arranged for a pharmaceutical company in New York to give the young man a job where he can learn the business. By letting the rumor run, Christian reveals how quickly the town's contempt turned to self-interested praise once money seemed involved and makes the would-be backers confront how little they actually knew about the boy they had dismissed.

episodes.title: On Wings Of Song (1940-06-19)
episodes.episodeDescription: Famous opera star Angela D'Nello returns to Rivers End, prompting Dr. Christian to remember the hometown moments that shaped her career. As a young singer she won a local music scholarship, and later, frozen by stage fright on an important opening night, Dr. Christian helped her find her voice by reminding her to sing as if she were back among the friends who first believed in her. Her bond with home is tested again when her mother becomes gravely ill while Angela is far away, making song the bridge that connects them across distance.

episodes.title: Suggestions For Divorce (1940-06-26)
episodes.episodeDescription: Joan Lyman's jealousy has driven her marriage to Steve toward divorce, especially after she becomes convinced he is involved with his secretary. Dr. Christian tells Joan that her suspicion helped create the very estrangement she feared and urges her to become again the woman Steve originally loved. When Joan and Christian unexpectedly meet Steve and the other woman at a restaurant, Christian forces the situation into the open instead of letting either side retreat. A discussion of divorce arrangements turns into a revealing quarrel, and Steve's companion decides she wants no part of the marriage or its baggage. With the outside relationship ended, Joan and Steve finally admit their own faults and reconcile before the divorce is completed.
