episodes.title: The Man Who Changed His Mind (1941-01-29)
episodes.displayTitle: The Man Who Changed His Mind (1941-01-29)
episodes.episodeDescription: Grocer Alex Johnson becomes furious when Dr. Christian quarantines his household after young Dickie contracts scarlet fever. Because Johnson runs a food store, the quarantine means he cannot simply live at home and continue working, and he declares that once the danger is past Christian will no longer be the family doctor. Weeks later the Johnson children play doctor in their backyard playhouse. They take real medicines from the house and give several pills and liquids to Dottie, then lock the playhouse as part of their game. When Christian learns what happened he breaks down the door, rushes the poisoned child to treatment and uses every antidote and stimulant he can while the family is being located. Johnson arrives still angry, believing Christian has interfered with his children yet again, only to discover the doctor is fighting to save his daughter. Dottie finally regains consciousness and passes the crisis. Faced with Christian's persistence and care despite having been dismissed, Johnson admits he was wrong, asks forgiveness and offers him a lifetime appointment as the Johnson family physician.

episodes.title: Sweethearts Protective Insurance (1942-09-16)
episodes.episodeDescription: Violet Lindsley is hurt when she learns that her California-based fiancé Harry Davis has bought a novelty policy promising him cash and a Hollywood date if she jilts him. Dr. Christian jokes that hometown sweethearts ought to organize protection of their own, but Judy turns the joke into a real Hometown Sweethearts Protective Insurance Company and it quickly attracts members and national attention. Hollywood publicity man Pete Wade arrives with an offer to send the first genuinely jilted member to Hollywood for a screen test. Harry interprets Violet's participation as proof that she distrusts him and breaks their engagement, technically making her the first eligible claimant. Violet refuses the glamorous trip because she wants Harry rather than publicity. Pete stays to persuade her, becomes increasingly charmed by Violet and small-town life, loses his studio job and converts the publicity idea into a permanent national organization based in Rivers End. By the end his assignment has become personal: he introduces Violet as the future Mrs. Pete Wade, and the two leave to obtain their marriage license with Dr. Christian chosen as best man.

episodes.title: An Artist Comes To Town (1942-09-23)
episodes.episodeDescription: When celebrated portrait painter Sylvia St. Vincent sweeps into Rivers End and demands the towns best doctor for an emergency, Dr. Christian discovers that the patient is her beloved dog rather than a person. After he successfully helps the animal, Sylvia insists on painting his portrait in gratitude. Dr. Christian accepts only on his own terms: instead of immortalizing him on canvas, he asks the famous artist to repaint an old table that belonged to his mother, and she turns the humble piece into a work of art.

episodes.title: On To Glory (1942-09-30)
episodes.episodeDescription: Aunt Tanny has no serious physical disease, but she has convinced herself that her time has come and has arranged her final days as carefully as a performance, calling in relatives, revising her will and taking comfort in a fully paid burial policy that promises a proper funeral. Dr. Christian realizes that the attention and drama surrounding death have become more appealing to her than recovery. He secretly has the burial policy removed just as Tanny appears ready to make her grand exit. The shock of discovering that her carefully planned funeral is no longer assured immediately rouses her anger, energy and will to live. Dr. Christian tells her she has suffered a rare malady requiring exactly such a shock and reminds her of the husband, blind brother, nieces and friends who still depend on her. Tanny abandons her trip to glory and begins recovering.

episodes.title: The Case Of Tommy Holms (1942-10-07)
episodes.episodeDescription: After attorney Gerald Fox deliberately crashes his car, he claims total amnesia just hours before a deadline for locating young Tommy Holmes, heir to a million-dollar estate. Dr. Christian becomes suspicious when Fox conveniently cannot identify the boy and discovers that Fox and the late mans business partner would profit if the heir is not confirmed in time. A supposed truth-drug injection is actually harmless distilled water, proving Fox has been faking his memory loss. Confronted, Fox identifies Tommy and signs the papers that secure the boys inheritance.

episodes.title: Black Magic (1942-10-14)
episodes.episodeDescription: Dr. Christian recalls a case in which Molly became ill after an asparagus dinner and developed a startling black discoloration of her mouth and tongue. Her doctor blamed poisoned food, and attorney Jernigan prepared a damage suit against grocer George Pullos for selling bad asparagus. Asked to investigate for the defense, Christian learns that Molly has also been taking a prescribed beef, iron and wine tonic. He realizes the dramatic black coloring is not proof of food poisoning at all: compounds in the asparagus react with the iron in the medicine and form a dark, ink-like color. Christian demonstrates the effect on himself in court by eating asparagus and taking the same tonic. The supposedly mysterious 'black magic' is exposed as an ordinary chemical reaction, the case against Pullos collapses, and Jernigan disappears rather than continue the failed claim.

episodes.title: Miss Lizzies Burglar (1942-10-21)
episodes.episodeDescription: Miss Lizzie surprises a burglar named Joe in her home, but instead of turning the injured man over to the police she nurses him back toward health. Joe, who boasts that he has avoided women all his life, becomes increasingly terrified that her kindness and concern mean she intends to marry him, and finally tries to escape before he is trapped. Dr. Christian is called into the absurd quarrel and discovers that both have misunderstood the other. Miss Lizzie has indeed been hoping to keep Joe, but not as a husband: what she desperately wants is a landscape gardener, and Joe happens to be one. The marriage panic collapses into a much more practical job offer.

episodes.title: Light On A Fallen Star (1942-10-28)
episodes.episodeDescription: Navy test pilot Grant Hopper survives a fiery crash without major physical injury, but afterward becomes terrified of flame, smoke, sudden noises and even ordinary reminders of flying. His fear turns him bitter and withdrawn from wife Helen and young daughter Dodie, whose admiration for her once-fearless father only deepens his shame. Dr. Christian recognizes that Grant's real injury is psychological and looks for a way to reconnect him with the courage and responsibility he believes he has lost. When Dodie is endangered by a fire, Grant rushes into the flames to save her. The rescue breaks the grip of the crash on him, and Grant realizes that in going into the fire for his daughter he recovered the part of himself he thought had been destroyed.

episodes.title: The Storm (1942-11-04)
episodes.episodeDescription: Discouraged after losing a patient he could not move to a properly equipped hospital, Dr. Christian broods over the money Rivers End lacks for specialists and better rural medical care. He falls asleep as a storm gathers and dreams that Dan Foster and his sister Blanche offer him a fortune to alter Blanche's face so she can impersonate a missing heiress and steal a million-dollar inheritance. The promised fee could finance nearly everything Christian has been wishing he could provide for his patients, making the temptation more dangerous than simple greed. He refuses the fraud, and Dan finally pulls a gun and threatens both Christian and Blanche unless the operation is performed. Christian still refuses. A crash of thunder wakes him before the gun can fire, and the dream leaves him reassured that limited resources do not excuse wrongdoing and that doing whatever good he can with what he has is still worthwhile.

episodes.title: Fields Of Corn (1942-11-11)
episodes.episodeDescription: World War I veteran Jim Brown is terrified that his only son Howard will volunteer for the Air Corps and endure the horrors that killed Jim's friends and left him with years of nightmares. He even offers Dr. Christian a thousand dollars to declare the healthy young man medically unfit, but the doctor refuses. Howard agrees to stay on the farm for his father's sake, despite wanting to serve and despite the support of the girl he plans to marry. During a violent night storm, Jim is shaken by what he describes as a dream or vision in which the corn outside seems to become the comrades who died beside him in the last war, calling on him not to make their sacrifice meaningless. By morning Jim has changed his mind and gives Howard his blessing to do what he believes is his duty.

episodes.title: Bottled Up (1942-11-18)
episodes.episodeDescription: A strange series of break-ins erupts around Riverâ€™s End as a desperate man searches drugstores and medical offices for bottles from a particular shipment. When he enters Dr. Christianâ€™s office and escapes with one bottle, the doctor notices that an identical bottle from the same delivery contains something hidden inside. He opens it and discovers a fountain pen with a rolled document concealed in its barrel. A call to the manufacturer reveals that a shipping clerk is suspected of stealing a valuable medical formula being prepared for the Army Medical Corps but had to be released for lack of evidence. Dr. Christian realizes the clerk hid the formula inside one bottle before shipment and is now frantically trying to recover the correct package after two similar shipments went to Riverâ€™s End. Police set a trap at another pharmacy and arrest him when he comes for the medicine. The hidden formula supplies the missing evidence, turning the local bottle-stealing mystery into a wartime case involving conspiracy against the federal government.

episodes.title: Antiques (1942-11-25)
episodes.episodeDescription: The proud Proctor sisters live in an old family mansion filled with heirlooms, but bedridden Jane does not realize how badly their finances have collapsed. Her sister Libby has been quietly selling treasured family pieces one by one to keep the household going, even parting with a desk that had belonged to their father and grandfather. Dr. Christian recognizes the desk in an antique shop and understands why Libby refused to open the mansion for a Red Cross tour and why she has become increasingly desperate. Rather than expose the secret to Jane, he finds a way to give the house a useful new life: Mrs. Dawson, the wife of a serviceman, and her two children desperately need room while the husband is away. Christian persuades the Proctors to take the family in, giving Jane companionship and purpose, bringing children and life back into the mansion, and easing the pressure that had been forcing Libby to sacrifice the family's past piece by piece.

episodes.title: We Hold These Truths (1942-12-02)
episodes.episodeDescription: Rivers End's civic leaders ask Dr. Christian to secure glamorous celebrities for a large War Bond rally, believing famous names are needed to push the local drive over the top. Christian agrees to provide 'stars,' but at the rally he explains that a town should not need show-business glamour to understand either the duty or the practical value of buying bonds. His guests are instead four servicemen: Sergeant Claude Baker, Corporal Stanley Winisaki, Private Streather and Private Swenson. Christian interviews them about their homes, backgrounds, reasons for serving and hopes for the future. One comes from a prosperous Boston family, another is the son of Polish immigrants, and the four different lives converge on ordinary ambitions, family, education and the constitutional liberty they are defending. By presenting them as the most important stars in America, Christian turns the rally from entertainment into a reminder of what the war effort is for. The example carries back into his own office, where he and Judy arrange to set aside ten percent of the practice's receipts and payroll for regular War Bond purchases.

episodes.title: Home Coming (1944-10-18)
episodes.episodeDescription: Combat pilot Nicky returns to his wife Connie physically recovered but emotionally unable to bear being close to her, even though he knows he still loves her. Dr. Christian traces the estrangement to survivor's guilt over Nicky's wingman Skip, who died after Nicky's aircraft went out of control during their last combat. Nicky has convinced himself that if he had recovered control sooner he might have saved Skip, and a confused vision during his own crash has become proof in his mind that Connie would be better off without him. When Connie later appears to be in danger near a washed-out bridge, Nicky's immediate terror for her safety breaks through the emotional numbness. He finds her unharmed on the road, embraces her and finally accepts that his love for her never disappeared, a reunion Dr. Christian describes as another miracle worked by love.

episodes.title: Fame Before Folly (1944-10-25)
episodes.episodeDescription: A widely reported rescue suddenly turns Dr. Christian from a quiet country physician into a national celebrity. Reporters, photographers, radio calls and even movie offers descend on Rivers End, and publicity man Scoop Gordon convinces himself that the doctor needs professional management. When Dr. Christian refuses to spend his time posing and endorsing products, Gordon secretly hires a close look-alike named Bottomley and manufactures photographs that appear to show the doctor promoting everything from baby products to girdles and dubious advice. The false publicity soon creates angry calls and absurd accusations from people who believe the endorsements are genuine. Confronted, Gordon admits the scheme, and Dr. Christian makes him hear the unglamorous truth behind the original rescue instead of the heroic legend Gordon wants to sell. The doctor returns to his patients, relieved to exchange manufactured fame for ordinary work.
episodes.plotSynopsis: A widely reported rescue suddenly turns Dr. Christian from a quiet country physician into a national celebrity. Reporters, photographers, radio calls and even movie offers descend on Rivers End, and publicity man Scoop Gordon convinces himself that the doctor needs professional management. When Dr. Christian refuses to spend his time posing and endorsing products, Gordon secretly hires a close look-alike named Bottomley and manufactures photographs that appear to show the doctor promoting everything from baby products to girdles and dubious advice. The false publicity soon creates angry calls and absurd accusations from people who believe the endorsements are genuine. Confronted, Gordon admits the scheme, and Dr. Christian makes him hear the unglamorous truth behind the original rescue instead of the heroic legend Gordon wants to sell. The doctor returns to his patients, relieved to exchange manufactured fame for ordinary work.

episodes.title: The Substitute (1944-11-01)
episodes.episodeDescription: Dr. Christian's overwork brings efficient nurse Agnes Spinney into the office as a temporary substitute for Judy. Spinney quickly reorganizes the office, changes long-standing suppliers, answers correspondence and assumes so many of Judy's duties that Judy feels she is being pushed aside. At the same time Judy is spending conspicuous hours with Lieutenant Tommy Bolton and helping shop for a wedding dress. Christian assumes Judy and Tommy are in love and decides that keeping Spinney will free Judy to marry and have a life of her own. Judy takes that decision as proof she has been replaced and walks out. At a community gathering Christian discovers that Tommy's real sweetheart is a blonde named Kay. Judy's secret errands with Tommy were actually helping him create a bust of Dr. Christian as the first memorial in Rivers End's new Hall of Humanity. Once the misunderstanding is cleared up, Judy returns to the office and Christian happily keeps his longtime partner beside him.

episodes.title: The Failure (1944-11-08)
episodes.episodeDescription: Jeff Fowler has recovered from a long illness but is unable to return to his former work, leaving him desperate to prove he can support his wife Alice and their children through writing. He pours himself into poetry and serious manuscripts, suffers rejection after rejection and comes to see himself as a miserable failure. During a visit, Dr. Christian hears Jeff improvise a fantasy adventure for the children and notices how completely the story captures them. He recognizes that Jeff's natural gift is not the literary form he has been forcing, but the children's stories he tells with ease and imagination. With Jeff's permission Christian acts as his representative and has those stories prepared for publication. He then reminds Jeff that Hans Christian Andersen also pursued other literary ambitions before his fairy tales became his lasting achievement. A publisher accepts Jeff's first collection of Winky and Blinky adventures, and Jeff finally understands that reaching the hearts of children is his real vocation rather than a failure.

episodes.title: Younger Generation (1944-11-15)
episodes.episodeDescription: Linda Munson learns that Lieutenant Alan Gibbons, the young man she had planned to marry before her mother objected that they were too young, has returned from war badly wounded and discouraged. She insists that she is old enough to decide where she belongs and goes to the military hospital with Dr. Christian. Alan is ashamed of his scarred face and has lost the will to continue treatment, but Lindas unwavering love convinces him that his future is not over. Their courage persuades the older generation, including Lindas mother, that the young people deserve more faith than they have been given.

episodes.title: Broken Melody (1944-11-22)
episodes.episodeDescription: A little girl named Carol brings her injured dog to Dr. Christian and leads him to her ailing mother, who has separated from an ambitious musician husband after the strain of his career and their hard life damaged her health. When the father follows them to Riverâ€™s End, he sees how much his family has suffered, admits that music had become more important to him than they were, and asks for a chance to put his wife and daughter first. Dr. Christian helps the family reconcile and begin again.

episodes.title: Juliet Said It (1944-11-29)
episodes.episodeDescription: Carol Tucker works as a nurse's aide while her husband, Sergeant Mark Tucker, serves overseas and her injured young brother-in-law Skip recovers in the hospital. Lonely and uncertain about Mark, Carol becomes fascinated by a glamorous visitor who presents himself as an RAF wing commander and former Russian prince. His stories and decorations impress the town, and after Mark is reported missing in action Carol begins to believe she may be falling in love with the supposed hero. Dr. Christian grows suspicious, especially after the man avoids a medical examination following an automobile accident. Skip's scrapbook of military decorations gives Christian the clue: the commander's claimed medal and the date he says he received it do not fit the actual history. Confronted, the impostor cannot produce proper papers and is taken by military police. Almost immediately a new War Department message reports that Mark is alive in a German prisoner-of-war camp and has been awarded the Silver Star for gallantry. Christian replaces the false hero at the town rally with the story of the real one, while Carol recognizes where her loyalty and love truly belong.

episodes.title: My Son (1944-12-06)
episodes.episodeDescription: Bachelor engineer Peter Mallison has barely moved into the old Decatur mansion when his houseboy finds a three-month-old baby abandoned on the doorstep during a storm. A note from the desperate mother identifies the child as little Jim and asks whoever lives in the beautiful house to be good to him; a young woman found collapsed nearby soon dies, apparently leaving the baby alone in the world. Peter initially insists that family life has no place in his plans, yet he becomes deeply attached to the child. When no suitable Rivers End home can be found, arrangements are made to send Jim to an orphanage in Perryville. Peter realizes too late that he cannot let the boy go, races the train by car, reaches Perryville and takes Jim back from the accompanying nurse, declaring the child his son. His next problem is providing a motherly home. Judy declines Peter's proposal that she leave her work to help raise the boy, so she introduces him to Abby Westing, a capable woman who loves children. Abby moves in to care for Jim, and within weeks she and Peter are so obviously falling in love that Christian and Judy expect the new family to end in marriage.

episodes.title: Such Things Dont Happen (1944-12-13)
episodes.episodeDescription: Mrs. Prince opposes her daughter Helen's marriage to recently discharged soldier Johnny Dodd because his family comes from the wrong side of the tracks, while proudly claiming descent from Revolutionary War hero Jonathan Jackson. Dr. Christian argues that Johnny's own service matters more than inherited social standing, but Mrs. Prince refuses to listen. Then Christian encounters Jonathan Jackson himself, apparently returned from the grave. The supposed family hero cheerfully dismantles the legend built around him: he was an ordinary man from an undistinguished family, his famous Revolutionary exploit was greatly exaggerated, and most decisively, he never married and therefore cannot be Mrs. Prince's ancestor at all. Christian brings Jonathan face to face with her. After hearing the truth from the man she has spent years glorifying, Mrs. Prince agrees to Helen and Johnny's marriage and promises them a proper wedding, while Jonathan disappears back into the night as mysteriously as he arrived.

episodes.title: The Fugitive (1944-12-20)
episodes.episodeDescription: An escaped prisoner in German uniform is shot near Rivers End on Christmas Eve, forcing Dr. Christian to decide whether wartime hatred can change a doctor's duty. He treats the wounded man and assists a mysterious visiting surgeon through a delicate operation, insisting that a patient must be cared for regardless of uniform. The apparent enemy is then identified as an American serviceman who had escaped a German prison camp wearing enemy clothing. The unknown surgeon departs before he can be thanked, while Dr. Christian concludes that the war may justify fighting the enemy's ideas but not abandoning a physician's obligation to an individual life.

episodes.title: Wish On A Star (1944-12-27)
episodes.episodeDescription: A rise in juvenile crime reaches Dr. Christian personally when a swaggering young tough named Joe comes to his office with a badly cut arm. Joe is trying to impress Judy Price with money, bravado and stories of easy living, but the doctor gradually learns that the cash comes from a gang involved in robberies. Joe wants out, yet the gangâ€™s hold and his fear of looking weak keep pulling him back. After an attempted holdup leaves him with a serious burn, Dr. Christian knows the police are already looking for a boy with exactly that injury. Joe begs the doctor not to turn him in because he wants Judy to remember him as someone worthwhile rather than as a criminal. Christian challenges him to prove that courage by surrendering voluntarily instead of waiting to be caught. Joe says an emotional goodbye to Judy, looks out at a star and makes his wish, then calls police headquarters himself and admits the holdup. Later Dr. Christian tells Judy that the judge recognized Joeâ€™s youth and voluntary confession, allowing him the chance to join the Navy and serve his country instead of simply disappearing into the criminal system.

episodes.title: The Queen Loved Herring (1945-01-10)
episodes.episodeDescription: Nurse Nina Jones falls in love with wealthy Army Air Forces lieutenant Jimmy Bradley but is ashamed to let him meet the immigrant grandparents who raised her in their small delicatessen home. Jimmy's family has asked him to meet Nina's people before making a promise, and Nina becomes convinced that the contrast in background will end the romance. Dr. Christian sends Jimmy to the house anyway, where the grandparents welcome him with their own food, wine and traditions. To break Nina's obsession with pedigree, the doctor tells an elaborate story about disguised royalty whose queen prized an ordinary herring above jewels, then admits privately that the tale is nonsense that served a useful purpose. Jimmy sees the worth of Nina's family for himself, and he and Nina promise that when the bells of peace ring they will also be wedding bells.

episodes.title: And Not To Yield (1945-01-17)
episodes.episodeDescription: Judy worries about a mysterious elderly man living quietly outside Rivers End with the devoted companion who has cared for him for years. The old man, once successful and well known, is now seriously ill and refuses help. Christian discovers that alcoholism destroyed his marriage long ago. His wife left with their young son Michael, and the ashamed father deliberately disappeared from the boy's life, believing that removing himself was the only decent thing he could still do. He later stopped drinking but remained too proud to seek forgiveness, following Michael's life only through photographs and clippings. Michael, now an Army lieutenant using his mother's surname Hill, has grown up believing his father simply abandoned him. Christian travels to Michael's camp and tells him the truth, arguing that older people can spend years paying inwardly for mistakes they made when they were younger. Michael at first refuses reconciliation, then changes his mind and returns to Rivers End. Father and son are reunited at the sickbed, and the old man's will to live returns with him. Their reconciliation closes with the lines from Tennyson that both remember: though weakened by time and fate, they remain strong in will 'to strive, to seek, to find, and not to yield.'

episodes.title: And A Little Child (1945-01-24)
episodes.episodeDescription: Marina leaves her brilliant surgeon husband Tony Bartlett after success and money turn him cold, arrogant and unwilling to treat patients who cannot pay. Military service changes Tony: working beside compassionate doctors among wounded servicemen teaches him why medicine exists and what his ambition had cost him. Back in Rivers End he uses his skill to save the orphaned child Jamie, reunites with Marina, and the couple decide to adopt the child, beginning a new family around service and love rather than status.

episodes.title: Always Yours (1945-01-31)
episodes.episodeDescription: After two years apart during the war, Gail Sloan breaks her engagement to serviceman Larry Warnock and becomes involved with older hospital doctor Graham, believing the distance has changed her feelings. Larry unexpectedly returns home suffering another attack of malaria and admits to Dr. Christian that losing Gail has left him with nothing to come home to. Meanwhile Graham pressures Gail into an immediate elopement across the state line. On the trip she realizes she has made a mistake, slips away from him at a bus stop and walks through the snow back to Rivers End. At Dr. Christian's office she and Larry finally speak honestly: he still wants a future with her, and she still loves him. Their reconciliation ends with Gail repeating the sign-off from Larry's wartime letters, 'always yours.'

episodes.title: The Shawl (1945-02-07)
episodes.episodeDescription: Civil War veteran Arthur Colby dies after spending most of his long life trying to remember a single wondrous event that occurred after he was wounded at Gettysburg. In one final lucid moment he can almost tell Dr. Christian what happened, recalling a hospital, terrible cold and something he must leave behind, but he dies before naming it. Convinced there is a record in Colby's abandoned house, Christian and Judy search it at night. Beneath the bed they find an old trunk containing a shawl, Colby's faded uniform and his wartime diary. The final entries solve the mystery. On July 6, 1863, as the wounded Colby lay outside a hospital shivering while waiting for space inside, a tall man stopped, removed the shawl from his own shoulders, wrapped it around the soldier and spoke kindly to him. The man was Abraham Lincoln. The shawl Colby had struggled all his life to remember was therefore not a forgotten romance, as Judy first imagined, but a personal relic of Lincoln's compassion. Christian and Judy realize they have recovered both the historic object and the memory Colby had wanted preserved.

episodes.title: Golden Bells (1945-02-14)
episodes.episodeDescription: Exhausted after a night with a sick child, Dr. Christian dozes in his office while worrying that he has promised a fresh story for a children's Valentine party. In his brief sleep he is summoned by a fairy from a second plane of existence and carried by magic carpet through a comic fantasy world of operators, trolls, fairies and strange rules to a golden palace where a young prince is in severe pain. Christian learns that the prince had visited the human world and eaten unripe apples. The court's mysterious magical illness turns out to be an ordinary stomachache, and a simple first-plane remedy quickly puts the prince right. The grateful fairy kingdom sends Christian home with a souvenir. He wakes after only a few minutes and tells Judy the whole impossible adventure as the new story for the children. Judy dismisses it as a dream, until Christian produces the physical souvenir he was given in the fantasy world.

episodes.title: George Washington Jenks (1945-02-21)
episodes.episodeDescription: Twelve-year-old George Washington Jenks is mocked by classmates for his name, glasses and refusal to fight, but the boys do not know that rheumatic fever left him with a serious heart condition that forbids strenuous activity. When they stage another humiliating prank, George finally fights back, collapses from the strain and nearly dies. Dr. Christian explains to the ashamed boys that George has been fighting all his life against physical handicaps and that enduring them without complaint has taken more courage than any schoolyard brawl. George recovers to find his classmates waiting to welcome him back and asking him to manage their team, turning the name they once ridiculed into one they respect.

episodes.title: The Laughingest Family (1945-04-25)
episodes.episodeDescription: Seven-year-old Mimi Peters has returned from wartime Europe after losing both parents and has passed through several foster homes without ever recovering the ability to laugh. Dr. Christian believes the traumatized child needs not another respectable placement but someone whose own suffering can create a genuine bond with her. At the same time, a young woman living in seclusion behind a black veil has withdrawn from the world because an accident scarred her face. Dr. Christian deliberately brings the two wounded lives together by arranging for Mimi to be lifted over the wall into the womanâ€™s garden. Mimi bluntly confronts the womanâ€™s shame, while the woman learns that Mimiâ€™s parents were killed in bombing and that the child believes her mother in heaven is waiting to hear her laugh again. Their defensiveness gives way to sympathy and affection. The woman removes her veil, decides to seek treatment for her scar and asks to adopt Mimi. Dr. Christian reveals that Mimiâ€™s supposed wandering into the garden was no accident, and the new family begins with both child and prospective mother ready to stop hiding from life.

episodes.title: This Is Where I Came In (1945-05-02)
episodes.displayTitle: This Is Where I Came In (1945-05-02)
episodes.episodeDescription: Returning serviceman Perry Tate is preparing to marry Mary Mason when actress Vivian Hall produces an old letter in Perry's handwriting that reads like a proposal to her. Perry explains that years earlier, while helping Vivian prepare props for a stage play, he copied the romantic letter directly from the script as a joke and signed it. Vivian nevertheless intends to use the document as proof of a promise to marry and as publicity to revive her career. Dr. Christian confronts her with a copy of the play and gets Vivian to reenact the scene in which the heroine burns the letter. Carried away by her own performance, Vivian accidentally sets fire to the real document. Christian puts out the fire, but Perry's signature has burned away, destroying the leverage Vivian meant to use against his real marriage plans.

episodes.title: Excalibur (1945-05-09)
episodes.episodeDescription: On a stormy night Dr. Christian tells Judy and Dick Foster a deliberately spooky story from a trip to Britain. He and two companions investigate a lake where local legend says Excalibur was cast away and is still guarded by the Lady of the Lake. A mysterious Lady Morgan in white seems to know more about their plans than she should, and when one of the men, Walker, makes a nighttime attempt to recover the sword, he dies in an accident that can be explained by a blow against the boat but leaves several uncanny details unresolved. Dr. Christian never tries again, leaving both the sword and the truth of the legend beneath the lake.

episodes.title: The Hero (1945-05-16)
episodes.episodeDescription: Riverâ€™s End is preparing to dedicate a monument to wartime hero John Blake, who is believed to have died after going down during the war and is credited locally with a Distinguished Service Cross. On the day of the ceremony Dr. Christian discovers a starving, bearded drifter and recognizes him as the supposedly dead John. John explains that he actually survived with the help of French peasants, but after earlier trouble with his commanding officer he failed to report back to the Army. The medal story was a mistake involving another serviceman named John Blake, and shame kept him from returning to a mother and sweetheart who believed he had died honorably. Dr. Christian warns that simply walking into the dedication as he is would destroy the pride that helped his mother endure her loss. episodes.title: Gentleman Of Mystery (1945-05-23)
episodes.episodeDescription: Famous author Gerald Halsey returns to Rivers End after years abroad intending to sell the family toolworks, whose new industrial process is important to the war effort. Bitter, detached from his family and contemptuous of patriotism, he seems willing to sell to a suspicious foreign buyer even after his son and young engineer Nick warn him about the danger. Dr. Christian secretly stages a confrontation with an actor posing as the foreign agent, complete with a planted witness and blank cartridge. When the fake buyer threatens the family, Halsey finally fights to defend his son and the process, revealing courage and loyalty he had buried beneath years of cynicism; Dr. Christian keeps the ruse private while Halsey begins reclaiming his place in the family.

episodes.title: General (1945-05-30)
episodes.episodeDescription: The elderly General Benjamin Gerard lives on wartime memories and meddles in the military letters received by his family, wanting to remain important while younger generations are away at war. After misplacing crucial letters and being harshly rebuked, he stages an apparent train accident so the family will fear losing him and appreciate him again. Dr. Christian quickly realizes the dramatic bruises are only ink, but lets the General keep his dignity rather than publicly exposing the ruse.

episodes.title: Diagnosis After Death (1945-06-06)
episodes.episodeDescription: While Dr. Alexander Webb is temporarily covering Dr. Christian's practice, state senator Fredericks is found dead in the street after appearing to stagger like a drunk. The senator's widow Margaret privately threatens Webb, saying she heard him quarrel with her husband shortly before the death and will accuse him of murder unless he helps prevent an investigation that could expose family scandals. Webb had opposed the senator's plan to release and abandon his violently insane brother, giving Margaret a plausible motive to use against him. At the medical inquiry, needle scars first suggest that the senator may have been a drug addict, but Webb notices that the fresh injection was high on the right arm, an awkward place for the right-handed senator to inject himself. He concludes the senator was diabetic, that the marks came from insulin, and that a family member sometimes gave the arm injections. An excessive dose would also explain the senator's staggering before death as insulin shock rather than drunkenness. As Webb works through the evidence, Margaret breaks down and confesses that she deliberately gave her husband the fatal overdose because she hated him. Her attempt to coerce and frame Webb collapses under the medical evidence.

episodes.title: Jere To Liebe (1945-06-13)
episodes.episodeDescription: With Dr. Christian away, Dr. Alexander Webb is drawn into the disappearance of visiting journalist Osgood, who had been seen anxiously studying an encyclopedia before vanishing to an abandoned quarry shack. Osgood is convinced that rapidly appearing red patches mean he has contracted leprosy and has isolated himself rather than expose his fiancee and the town. Webb traces the clue to the encyclopedia volume, examines him and finds that the terrifying self-diagnosis is completely wrong: after months of sparse wartime eating, rich food has triggered an extreme case of hives. The frightened reporter returns to Rivers End cured of both the rash and his imagined fatal disease, with his wedding merely postponed while he recovers.

episodes.title: The Lady The Wolf (1945-06-20)
episodes.episodeDescription: While Dr. Alexander Webb is temporarily filling in at Rivers End, Judy Price keeps receiving bold telephone calls from Marine Lieutenant Jerry Mitchell, a stranger who has been told about her by a mutual friend. Webb dismisses Jerry as a telephone wolf and warns Judy against meeting him, but Jerry turns out to be a decent, lonely serviceman spending his last night of leave in town. Judy agrees to go dancing with him, leaving Webb with Jerry's unused concert tickets. Webb then telephones a woman he barely knows to offer the tickets and, in the process, gets himself invited to accompany her. Later Judy and Jerry run into Webb and his new companion at the concert, where Webb's attempt to pretend he is a classical-music expert quickly collapses. The comedy leaves Judy amused that the man who lectured her about telephone wolves has been caught in essentially the same sort of spontaneous romance himself.

episodes.title: Dr. Christian Award Winners of 1945 (1945-06-27)
episodes.episodeDescription: This special broadcast steps away from the usual Riverâ€™s End drama to announce the winners of the 1945 Dr. Christian script competition. Jean Hersholt first reports on his just-completed trip to war-torn Europe and Denmark, then the program names eight prize-winning writers selected on merit from thousands of entries. The $2,000 first prize goes to Eleanor Tarshis of Forest Hills, New York; Joseph C. Cook and Dr. Simon G. Sacks of Duluth share the $1,000 second prize; James Boston of Cambridge receives the $500 third prize; and five additional writers receive $350 awards. The broadcast interviews several winners, including Tarshis in the studio and Cook and Sacks by remote connection from Duluth, discussing how they came to radio writing and developed their entries. The show closes by previewing upcoming broadcasts of the winning plays, making this episode a behind-the-scenes awards program rather than a fictional Dr. Christian story.

episodes.title: Always A Woman (1945-07-11)
episodes.episodeDescription: Mike Taylor has waited for his fiancee to come home on leave from the Women's Army Corps, but when she arrives as a confident lieutenant he feels diminished by comparison and begins pushing her away. She interprets his defensiveness as rejection and prepares to leave Rivers End for good. Dr. Christian recognizes that Mike is not ashamed of her service; he is ashamed of how inadequate he feels beside it. He disables his own car and arranges for Mike to drive her on an out-of-town medical errand, giving them the private time neither has managed to ask for. The operation succeeds: she later telephones as Mrs. Michael Taylor.

episodes.title: Joyous Heart (1945-07-18)
episodes.episodeDescription: Margaret Powers leaves the hospital convinced that her serviceman husband Hal has finally come home, only for Dr. Christian to discover that the bouquet she thought he brought was actually a telegram reporting him missing. He gently helps her face the shock without stripping away every source of hope. When fresh cigar ashes appear in Hals locked room, Margaret knows there is an ordinary explanation, but accepts them as the tangible sign she needs to believe he may still return, and the renewed hope restores her strength.

episodes.title: The Liar (1945-07-25)
episodes.episodeDescription: Lydia Parker returns to Rivers End after years away and asks Dr. Christian for help with her twin sister Lucy. Lydia says Lucy has become a compulsive liar, inventing pointless stories about where she has been, what she has done and whom she has seen, and that the behavior has worsened since the death of Lucy's husband Emil. Christian listens carefully as Lydia describes their lifelong closeness and insists that Lucy is physically healthy but emotionally disturbed. He suggests rest and familiar surroundings and avoids directly challenging Lydia's account. Only after Lydia leaves again, supposedly taking Lucy to relatives in California, does the truth emerge: Lucy died of pneumonia in the spring of 1901, nearly forty years earlier, and Christian himself was a pallbearer at her funeral. Lydia never accepted her twin's death and has continued to live as though Lucy were beside her, creating new stories to explain her supposed activities. Because Lydia remains harmless and otherwise functions normally, Christian chooses compassion over a brutal confrontation with the fantasy, arguing that the lonely woman's private reality deserves understanding rather than ridicule.

episodes.title: The Legend Of Khorassam (1945-08-01)
episodes.episodeDescription: While resting between calls, Dr. Christian is startled by a mysterious woman who brings an urgently ill companion, Moses, into his office. An emergency operation saves the man and removes an enormous pearl-like object that had been obstructing his airway. The strangers depart almost as mysteriously as they arrived, leaving Dr. Christian with an unexplained gift and a story that seems to echo an old legend; rather than destroy the mystery by investigating too closely, he chooses to let a little wonder remain.

episodes.title: Christmas Deferred (1945-08-08)
episodes.episodeDescription: Six-year-old Ted Ward was gravely ill and unconscious through the previous Christmas, and his mother Ruth has never told him that the holiday passed while he slept. Ruth has also cut herself and Ted off from Rivers End, embittered by the disgrace and death of her husband Glenn after he took money from a bank and, she believes, was never given a chance to make restitution. When Dr. Christian learns that Ted is waiting for a Christmas he thinks is still ahead, he and newspaper editor Matt Redding decide to give it to him in midsummer. Matt publishes Ted's story and August 8 becomes a community Christmas, drawing gifts, letters, a tree and old neighbors who rediscover their own generosity. Christian deliberately shows Ruth how the project is healing other wounded people too, including an elderly craftsman who resumes making toys after losing his son in the war and former enemies who reconcile while baking Christmas cookies. Ruth's resistance finally breaks as she sees Ted brighten and the town answer bitterness with kindness. When Ted's grandmother tries to remove him from the excitement, Ted insists the celebration is helping him. Afterward he admits to Christian that he eventually realized it was August, not December, but continued the make-believe because the unusual Christmas was doing as much good for his mother and grandmother as it was for him.

episodes.title: Canine Justice (1945-08-15)
episodes.episodeDescription: Young Teddy Douglas is devoted to Laddie, the family's discharged K-9 Corps dog whose wartime training makes him far more than an ordinary pet. Exploring an abandoned house that neighborhood children consider haunted, Teddy discovers a wanted jewel thief hiding there with stolen property. The fugitive catches the boy, ties him up and plans to leave him helpless while he escapes. Teddy warns that Laddie will come when called, and when the armed criminal threatens the dog, Laddie attacks and subdues him badly enough for the police to capture him. The thief survives and is identified as a man wanted in several cities, making Teddy eligible for a substantial reward. When officials then discuss destroying Laddie because he attacked a human being, Dr. Christian insists the dog used the training given him in war to save a child's life and help bring a dangerous criminal to justice, and vows to fight any attempt to punish him for it.

episodes.title: Leave It To Love (1945-08-22)
episodes.episodeDescription: Randy Foster returns to Rivers End after losing both feet in combat. Army rehabilitation has taught him to use artificial feet confidently, he is preparing to return to work, and he wants an ordinary life rather than constant reminders that he is different. His wife Ellen, however, cannot stop protecting him, worrying over steps, drafts, traffic and every small exertion until her sympathy becomes suffocating. Randy asks Dr. Christian to help her see that he is capable, while Ellen separately complains that Randy refuses the special care she thinks he needs. Christian mischievously turns the situation around so that each begins treating the other as the fragile one. Randy fusses over Ellen, insists she rest and takes over the household, while Ellen experiences firsthand how oppressive excessive solicitude can feel. The scheme collapses when Christian and Judy arrive and learn the real reason Ellen has not been feeling well: she is pregnant. With a baby genuinely on the way, the couple's roles and worries find a more natural balance, and Christian admits that love and nature have solved the problem better than his meddling could.

episodes.title: Puff (1945-08-29)
episodes.episodeDescription: Young Ted was blinded during a bombing in France that killed his family, and he insists that his beloved white poodle Puff still visits and guides him even though no one else can see the dog. X-rays reveal a treatable brain injury, but after successful surgery Ted still cannot see, leading Dr. Christian to suspect that fear and grief are blocking the recovery. When Ted's father, previously reported missing in action, unexpectedly returns, Ted finally uses his eyes and recognizes him. The father then tells how a mysterious white poodle led him safely through a German minefield, eerily echoing Ted's stories of Puff and leaving the dog's true nature unexplained.

episodes.title: Much To Do About Marty (1945-09-05)
episodes.episodeDescription: Laurie Gary separates from her bandleader husband Marty after years of having their private life turned into material for his jokes, while Marty resents Laurie's increasingly determined effort to make him quieter, more dignified and socially conventional. Dr. Christian compares them to children in a tug of war and suggests that Marty stop pulling back for a while. Marty therefore gives Laurie exactly the refined husband she says she wants, trading his usual gags and show-business energy for quiet evenings, classical reading and restraint. The experiment makes both of them see what they have been demanding from the other. After Laurie gets a closer look at how difficult Marty's comic work really is, Marty promises not to exploit everything she says for a gag, and Laurie promises not to be so sensitive about the humor that is part of him. They reconcile without either having to become someone else.

episodes.title: Room Clerk (1945-09-12)
episodes.episodeDescription: When Charlie Stutz, the room clerk on the three-to-eleven shift at Rivers End's United States Hotel, suffers a heart attack, Dr. Christian is summoned and sends him to the hospital. The hotel manager is away in Chicago and Alex, the next clerk, has not reported for work, leaving a lobby full of guests with no one to handle keys, mail, telephones or room problems. Bellboy George persuades Christian to take over the desk temporarily, with Judy helping, and the doctor quickly discovers that hotel work can be as chaotic as medicine. He sorts out wrong keys, confused guests and a drunken occupant while trying to find a room for a soldier's mother who has arrived late at night to meet her son when he comes home on furlough the next day. With every room occupied, Christian has the drunk guest moved to a warm cot in the furnace room under the pretense that the boys are hiding him from the police, freeing his room for the mother. Alex finally returns and, impressed that Christian kept the hotel running, relieves him. Christian and Judy are barely out the door when George calls them back because a woman in room 308 is having a baby, sending the exhausted doctor straight from his temporary job as room clerk back into his real profession.

episodes.title: Our Daughter Barbara (1945-09-19)
episodes.episodeDescription: Laura Marshall is deeply devoted to her husband Steve and to Barbara, Steve's daughter from his first marriage, but a man from Laura's past threatens the family. Before coming to Rivers End, Laura had fallen in love with married Carl Gilbert and, after discovering he never intended to leave his wife, drove her car through a guardrail in despair. She recovered, began a new life and later married Steve. Months into that marriage, however, Laura angrily went out with Carl one night after quarreling with Steve because he would not leave an ill Barbara to take Laura on a trip. Carl later returns broke and demands $5,000. He still has Laura's old love letters and threatens to combine them with evidence of that night out to persuade Barbara's bitter maternal grandmother, who once lost a custody fight with Steve, to reopen the case by portraying Laura as an unfit stepmother. Unable to raise the money without Steve learning why, Laura turns to Dr. Christian. Christian brings Carl and Steve together and forces the blackmail into the open. Steve is initially shocked and Laura, believing he values her only as a mother for Barbara, prepares to leave. At that moment Steve recognizes that he loves Laura herself as much as ever. He stops her, forgives her, and they return home together to Barbara, while Carl's leverage disappears.

episodes.title: The Wolf Cried Navy Blue (1945-09-26)
episodes.episodeDescription: Navy sailors Joe and Pip miss their train after Joe jumps off in Rivers End chasing a woman he mistakes for an old sweetheart. Dr. Christian and Judy invite the stranded sailors to dinner, where both men become increasingly interested in Judy and turn the evening into a comic rivalry full of boasting, flirting and misunderstandings. By the time they finally make the next train, the supposedly quiet town has given Judy exactly the kind of unexpected adventure she had been wishing for.

episodes.title: Love To Mama (1945-10-03)
episodes.episodeDescription: Madeleine Renaldi's elderly mother lives for letters from her absent son Johnny, the troubled child she has always loved most. Mama believes Johnny escaped his criminal past, found honest work in California and is saving for a fur coat and a home where she can live with him. Madeleine knows the truth but protects the illusion: she reads the letters, destroys the evidence Mama should not see, goes hungry to buy the promised fur coat herself and lets Mama credit Johnny for everything. The truth finally arrives in a letter Mama brings to Dr. Christian to read aloud. Johnny has spent months in prison and is about to die in the electric chair. Realizing too late that Mama is hearing every word, Dr. Christian then explains Madeleine's sacrifice, including finding her praying in the snow for Johnny's soul. Mama understands that her daughter's supposed jealousy was love and courage, and chooses to keep sharing the comforting fiction with Madeleine rather than let the truth destroy what they have left.
episodes.plotSynopsis: Madeleine Renaldi's elderly mother lives for letters from her absent son Johnny, the troubled child she has always loved most. Mama believes Johnny escaped his criminal past, found honest work in California and is saving for a fur coat and a home where she can live with him. Madeleine knows the truth but protects the illusion: she reads the letters, destroys the evidence Mama should not see, goes hungry to buy the promised fur coat herself and lets Mama credit Johnny for everything. The truth finally arrives in a letter Mama brings to Dr. Christian to read aloud. Johnny has spent months in prison and is about to die in the electric chair. Realizing too late that Mama is hearing every word, Dr. Christian then explains Madeleine's sacrifice, including finding her praying in the snow for Johnny's soul. Mama understands that her daughter's supposed jealousy was love and courage, and chooses to keep sharing the comforting fiction with Madeleine rather than let the truth destroy what they have left.

episodes.title: Chain Letter (1945-10-10)
episodes.episodeDescription: Dr. Christian and Judy argue over why people perpetuate chain letters, with Christian blaming fear and Judy believing money is the stronger motive. To test the question they send one to their financially struggling friend Tom Holland, whose advertising agency is close to failure. Tom himself despises chain letters, but his superstitious wife Bertha secretly sends copies in hopes of bringing him luck. One copy is addressed in Tom's name to Jack Douglas, the Old Silver cigarette representative whose account Tom desperately needs, even though Douglas has just declared that people who send chain letters are fools. Tom, Bertha, Christian and Judy scramble to recover the damaging letter. In the middle of the crisis, however, the repeated idea of a chain gives Tom the advertising hook he has been unable to find: a slogan linking chain smoking with Old Silver cigarettes. Douglas loves the campaign and awards Tom the major account, joking that he knew Tom was intelligent when Tom said he had thrown a chain letter away. The experiment nearly ruins Tom, but the chain letter accidentally supplies the idea that saves his business.

episodes.title: The Attic Stairway Murder Mystery (1945-10-17)
episodes.episodeDescription: When wealthy Mrs. Parker is found dead at the bottom of her attic stairs, suspicion falls on her disabled housekeeper and former friend Mary Bignall, especially after Mrs. Parkers rings disappear. Dr. Christian learns that decades earlier Mrs. Parker had intercepted and switched letters between Mary and Ed Parker, then married Ed after an accident left Mary crippled. On the day of the death Mary finally found Eds original Valentine proving he had never rejected her; during their confrontation Mrs. Parker lost her balance and fell. Mary arranged the body and took the rings Ed had once meant for her, but Dr. Christian chooses to let the accidental death and Marys long suffering remain private.

episodes.title: Playboy (1945-10-24)
episodes.episodeDescription: Pat Blair has always been Rivers End's charming, irresponsible playboy, and a damaged heart has kept him out of military service while his old schoolmate Bob Sims fights overseas. Gossip becomes especially ugly when Pat spends time with Bob's wife Lily, leading Bob to write Lily that she need not remain tied to him if she prefers Pat. Then Pat is injured in an automobile accident after trying to avoid blind Elizabeth Elliott as she crosses the street; Elizabeth suffers a broken hip and fears she will never walk again. Dr. Christian sends Pat to cheer her, and the supposedly selfish playboy devotes himself to her recovery. He helps arrange her settlement, sells securities left by his mother to pay part of it himself, tends her garden and becomes the one person who can make her laugh and believe she will walk. Bob returns on furlough just as Lily unexpectedly finds Pat coaching Elizabeth through her first steps. Lily angrily condemns Pat, but Elizabeth defends the friend she has come to know. The emotional confrontation makes Elizabeth forget her fear long enough to walk, while Bob finally hears Lily's explanation and recognizes how badly gossip and assumption distorted what happened. Christian's lesson is that Pat contains real generosity despite his faults, and that judging any of them by reputation alone misses the whole person.

episodes.title: Sterling Silver (1945-10-31)
episodes.episodeDescription: As Rivers End's old opera house is about to be demolished, Dr. Christian remembers Sterling Silver, the melodrama actor who was his boyhood hero. The past suddenly becomes a real mystery when owner Sam Roberts is shot, valuable antique playbills disappear and one of Silver's ornate pistols is found at the scene. Sam believes the now-elderly actor attacked him over a thirty-thousand-dollar promissory note, but Dr. Christian cannot reconcile that accusation with the man he remembers. Returning to the dark theater with police, he traps the real thief, who had clubbed Silver, stolen one of his pistols, accidentally shot Sam and hidden both Silver and the stolen playbills among the stage props. Silver survives, the old debt is explained as an investment gone bad rather than a betrayal, and Dr. Christian gets one final chance to remember the theater as it was before demolition.

episodes.title: The Last Awakening (1945-11-07)
episodes.episodeDescription: After a flood, scores of Rivers End residents suddenly fall into a deep, unnatural sleep, filling the hospital and provoking an airtight quarantine around the town. Dr. Christian notices that the victims are medically normal and traces the mystery to the waterworks, where Mayor Andrews personally tried to replenish a depleted chlorine supply. In the rush, cylinders of chloral were mistaken for chlorine; mixed into the water, the chemical formed chloral hydrate, effectively dosing the town with a powerful sleeping drug. Once the accidental contamination is identified, the terrifying epidemic is revealed to be a massive but temporary poisoning rather than a new disease.

episodes.title: The Long Lane (1945-11-14)
episodes.episodeDescription: Gladys Brooks has built a new life with her young son Jackie and plans to marry Jerry Connor after years of separation from her husband Jeffrey. A War Department telegram suddenly reports that Jeffrey, long believed lost, has been found alive in China. Jackie is thrilled to learn that his father served in the war, while Gladys is forced to face feelings she thought were over. When Jeffrey returns, crippled but changed, he tells Dr. Christian that he had left Gladys because he believed he was selfish and useless, then found purpose fighting in China and learned to live for other people. Convinced Gladys loves Jerry, Jeffrey plans to leave rather than stand in her way. Gladys overhears him, realizes she still loves her husband, and asks his forgiveness. Jerry quietly withdraws as the separated couple reunites and Jackie gets his father back.

episodes.title: The Philandering Ghost (1945-11-21)
episodes.episodeDescription: Recently discharged veteran John Talbot reopens his family's supposedly haunted old house, where the legend of his vanished great-uncle Mortimer soon becomes very lively. A flirtatious 'ghost' begins kissing frightened women, and John discovers that Mortimer has been wandering because of a promise made after losing the woman he loved. The supernatural visitor's matchmaking creates comic chaos but ultimately helps bring new affection into the lonely house, leaving John with the chance to replace the old haunting with life, love and laughter.

episodes.title: Retreat To Kindness (1945-11-28)
episodes.episodeDescription: Former Rivers End troublemaker Jim Bradley returns as a successful, hard-edged reporter determined to write a sensational feature on psychiatrist Dr. Bob Patterson. Bradley plans to expose the violence and mental illness in Patterson's childhood home, including his father's commitment to an institution and young Patterson's own brief jailing after striking his father while defending his mother. Christian, Judy and Patterson argue that publishing every painful fact would serve gossip more than truth and would needlessly hurt Patterson's elderly mother, but Bradley prides himself on having no sentimentality and insists that hurting people is sometimes part of being a good reporter. Bradley has also returned to collect the diary his own mother left for him, sealed away after her death. Reading it changes him: his mother wrote of her love for Jim and of her gratitude to Patterson for helping her understand that Jim needed to leave Rivers End and make his own life, even though she longed to call him home. Confronted with the private compassion he had dismissed in others, Bradley abandons the article and tells Christian he is leaving with something more important, having made his own 'retreat to kindness.'

episodes.title: Girl Trouble (1945-12-05)
episodes.episodeDescription: A cold December night brings Dr. Christian into what first looks like an attempted kidnapping. Wealthy schoolboy Johnny is found bound, gagged and nearly frozen on the Ramseysâ€™ porch, and the police assume a gang of boys must be responsible. Dr. Christian is less convinced. He sees that Johnny is under intense pressure from parents who buy him everything but give him little freedom, demand top school performance, control his food and schedule, and leave almost no time for ordinary play. Johnny also has a very obvious adolescent interest in the Ramseysâ€™ pretty daughter Marie. As the boy recovers, Dr. Christian establishes that the crude ropes and wire were no professional kidnapping tools and finally gets to the truth: Johnny staged the incident himself. Rather than punish a frightened and embarrassed boy, the doctor makes his parents recognize how their expectations helped drive him to such a desperate bid for attention. He persuades the police and family to let the matter die quietly, then asks Marie to help Johnny put the episode behind him by refusing to feed further gossip.

episodes.title: Susan Comes Marching Home (1945-12-12)
episodes.episodeDescription: Riverâ€™s End welcomes home Army nurse Susan Anderson, who has survived wartime service and years in a Japanese prison camp. Susan has only thirty days of leave before returning to duty, and she has already decided what she wants most: to marry Hillary Dana, the shy lumber-mill owner she has loved since their school days. Hillary loves Susan too, but feels inadequate beside a decorated Army captain and is so painfully bashful that every attempt to propose collapses into comic disaster. Dr. Christian and Judy repeatedly try to coach him, but even a carefully rehearsed visit ends with a broken goldfish bowl and Hillary fleeing without his hat. Convinced he has made a fool of himself, Hillary retreats to a fishing cabin he had quietly begun building for Susan after wartime reports made him fear she would never come home. Susan finds him there, forces the truth into the open and accepts his clumsy proposal. Dr. Christian arrives with one more piece of good news: the Army is releasing personnel who spent more than sixty days in prison camps, so Susanâ€™s discharge will allow the couple to begin their life together without another separation.

episodes.title: The Little Carpenter (1945-12-19)
episodes.episodeDescription: Dr. Christian is unexpectedly left to host an elegant Christmas party where old resentments and hidden scandals quickly surface. A wealthy man revives a decades-old grievance against the woman who rejected him when he was poor, her naval-officer son is exposed for borrowing valuable securities he could not repay, and another young man reveals that he and the officer are twin brothers separated in childhood, one adopted into privilege while the other grew up poor. The bitterness is interrupted by a poor boy asking to earn enough money for a set of carpenter's tools. His simple Christmas appeal changes the room: the overlooked brother offers the value of his art scholarship to cover the debt, the injured businessman chooses forgiveness and honest repayment, the officer's fiancée stands by him, and the adults begin reconciling. At dinner they discover that the little boy has quietly returned the money they gave him, completing the lesson in generosity.

episodes.title: Mission Accomplished (1945-12-26)
episodes.episodeDescription: Ten-year-old Joni Love has taken seriously the last assignment her father gave her before he was killed during the war: look after her mother and make sure she is happy. Deciding that her lonely mother needs another husband, Joni first asks bachelor Dr. Christian to marry her. He gently declines but agrees to help. The better prospect turns out to be returning Major Miller, owner of the local radio station that Leslie Love has competently managed during his military service. Because their correspondence was signed simply 'Leslie Love,' Miller had assumed his wartime station manager was a man and initially has difficulty accepting that a woman has run the operation so well. Meeting Leslie quickly changes his attitude. Joni notices that her mother likes the younger major and that he likes both mother and daughter, and cheerfully shifts her matchmaking plan from Dr. Christian to Miller, satisfied that she is finally carrying out her father's mission to keep her mother from being alone.

episodes.title: What It Takes (1946-01-02)
episodes.episodeDescription: A January blizzard strands Dr. Christian, Judy and a cross-section of strangers on an interurban bus. Among them are a wounded veteran disgusted by civilian complaining, a prisoner being returned under guard, a struggling musician, and a young mother whose undernourished baby urgently needs milk. Dr. Christian discovers that the mother is also clinging to the belief that her husband will come home, although the military telegram she carries reports him killed. As the stalled bus grows colder, the passengers who had been arguing and thinking only of themselves begin giving up coats, blankets, comfort and safety to protect the mother and child. Men set out through the storm for help, and even the prisoner, given a genuine opportunity to run, chooses not to escape. By morning the crisis has shown each of them what it takes to put another person's life ahead of his own grievances.

episodes.title: Curare (1946-01-09)
episodes.episodeDescription: Former star aerialists Benning and Brown come to Dr. Christian with progressive weakness, dizziness and failing grip that have reduced them from the big time to a small circus. He warns them not to perform until the illness is understood, but they go on anyway and one falls from the trapeze. At the ring Dr. Christian notices clown Jojo drop a small bottle and connects it with the performers' rope-burned bare hands. Testing the equipment reveals that their trapeze ropes have been repeatedly dosed with curare, slowly poisoning the men through contact. Jojo confesses that he trained Benning and Brown, then grew bitter when they became stars while an injury ended his own aerial career. His elaborate revenge had been to destroy them gradually while pretending to remain their loyal friend.

episodes.title: Scandal In The Fourth Dimension (1946-01-16)
episodes.episodeDescription: Professor John Boswell refuses to approve his daughter Betty's marriage to young Alec Dale because Alec intends to become an inventor after leaving the Army. Rather than argue directly, Dr. Christian tells Boswell an outrageous college story about Professor Erasmus Doke, his brilliant student Aloysius O'Flannigan and Doke's daughter Patsy. In Christian's tale, Doke's experiments with the fourth dimension leave him only partly visible. Aloysius understands the mathematics well enough to restore him, but will help only if Doke accepts his courtship of Patsy. Doke stubbornly refuses and tries to live half-invisible, producing classroom chaos, public panic and an absurd arrest in which police struggle with the visible and invisible halves of him. Humiliated, Doke finally gives in, Aloysius restores him, and the young couple's engagement follows. Boswell suspects Christian invented the whole story, but the lesson works: he admits he may have been too hard on Alec and agrees to reconsider rather than trying to stop the younger generation from choosing for itself.

episodes.title: Mr Sourpuss (1946-01-23)
episodes.episodeDescription: Children's author and illustrator Elliott Kenyon returns from wartime service physically recovering from a bomber crash but emotionally shut down, hiding under another name and insisting that he can never write again. He finally tells Dr. Christian why: during his last mission over a French town, the bombing killed the mother of a little boy whose family later sheltered the wounded Elliott. The memory has made his old cheerful stories seem impossible and leaves him feeling unworthy of nurse Ann, who loves him. Time with Ann's young niece Candy begins to reopen the part of Elliott that could draw and tell stories, and he produces his first successful sketch since the war. Then Candy's father is killed in an accident overseas and the child runs away in grief. Elliott helps find her and reads the final letter her father left, urging Candy not to turn away from life because the world contains pain but to help make her own part of it worth living. The message speaks directly to Elliott's own guilt. By comforting Candy he finally accepts that he too must keep living, writing and loving, and he commits himself to a future with Ann and Candy.

episodes.title: Miss Minnie (1946-01-30)
episodes.episodeDescription: After Dr. Christian persuades merchant J.D. Carter to give the formerly sheltered Minnie Marvin a job, Carter becomes convinced Minnie is trying to marry him. He secretly reads her diary, interprets every romantic entry as being about himself and grows so desperate to escape that he enlists in the Navy. Christian is less certain Carter has identified the right man. The truth arrives when Minnie announces that she is marrying James Sheldon, the postman she has loved for months. She also reveals that her father left her forty thousand dollars and that she has already bought the couple a home, but she kept the inheritance quiet because she wanted to work and wanted to know she was loved for herself rather than her money. Carter is left with a needless naval enlistment and the entire town's laughter at his vanity.

episodes.title: Requiem For A Hero (1946-02-06)
episodes.episodeDescription: Father John Mulligan visits a condemned murderer who uses the same name and is wearing a unique family ring. The priest realizes the prisoner may be the infant son he believed lost at sea decades earlier, before he entered the priesthood. Dr. Christian questions the man, who claims the ring belonged to another rescued child named Eddie Graham and convinces Father John that Eddie, later a decorated serviceman killed in the South Pacific, was his true son. After the priest leaves comforted, Dr. Christian exposes the prisoner's deception: the man himself was the baby from the lifeboat and used an old photograph from the parcel to describe Father John's wife. Facing death, he chose to give his father a heroic son to remember rather than the shame of knowing a murderer was his child. Dr. Christian keeps the secret and tells him that his sacrifice was itself an act of heroism.

episodes.title: The Hoofer (1946-02-13)
episodes.episodeDescription: Successful dancer Evangeline Moore returns to Rivers End exhausted and refuses ever to dance again. Years earlier she and her partner and fiancé Johnny 'Skeeter' Briggs were on the verge of a major stage break when he was inducted into the Army. Evangeline later toured for servicemen with the USO, but after Johnny's letters stopped she became convinced he was dead and finally collapsed into grief and self-pity. Dr. Christian traces Johnny and learns that he survived the war with a disabling injury. Believing Evangeline should not be tied to a helpless man, Johnny deliberately stayed silent while undergoing months of rehabilitation and dance practice. Dr. Christian arranges for Evangeline to attend a wounded-soldiers hospital show where Johnny makes his first public dancing appearance since his injury. The two reunite, discover that neither has stopped loving the other, and decide to dance together again.

episodes.title: The Girl With The Golden Gauntlets (1946-02-20)
episodes.displayTitle: The Girl With The Golden Gauntlets (1946-02-20)
episodes.episodeDescription: Dr. Christian remembers Paris before the war, when his wealthy, aimless friend Steve became infatuated with the celebrated beauty Ariella, famous for never removing long golden gloves. Suspicious of her reputation and curious about the secret beneath the gloves, Steve and Dr. Christian trick Ariella into exposing hands that are badly deformed. Horrified by the cruelty of what he has done, Steve abandons his idle life and devotes himself to medicine, becoming a renowned plastic surgeon. Years later Dr. Christian reveals that the glamorous woman visiting Rivers End is Ariella herself, now Steve's wife, and that Steve's career was driven by his determination to restore the hands he once shamed her for hiding.

episodes.title: Forbidden Hill (1946-02-27)
episodes.episodeDescription: Fourteen years after seven schoolchildren died from poison placed in a well at Cedar Hill, Margaret Anderson returns to Riverâ€™s End with her brother Roderick, the man who was blamed for the crime and committed to an asylum. Dr. Christian has always doubted that Roderick was insane, but the town still remembers him as a killer. Margaret repeatedly calls the doctor to the decaying house, while Roderick angrily tries to keep him away and appears to be threatening his sister. During a later visit Margaret serves Dr. Christian and Judy poisoned tea, but Roderick bursts in and knocks it from their hands, apparently attacking them. Laboratory testing confirms the poison and reverses the apparent roles. Dr. Christian concludes that Margaret, not Roderick, poisoned the children years earlier and is still dangerously disturbed. Roderick had understood his sisterâ€™s condition and silently accepted suspicion and confinement rather than expose her. His violent-looking intervention at Cedar Hill was actually another attempt to protect innocent people from her, finally giving Dr. Christian the proof needed to clear the man he never believed was insane.

episodes.title: One For The Money (1946-03-06)
episodes.episodeDescription: Eighty-five-year-old Harriet Petticord summons her three young heirs and recruits Dr. Christian and Judy for a test of character. Although still wealthy, Harriet has Christian tell them that bad investments have left her penniless and that her house and belongings must be sold. Her grandniece Carol, a struggling actress and playwright, is prepared to help, while Carol's twin brother Bill cannot come because he is in the Army and sends his friend Private Frank Kennedy with a letter. Cousin Roger, Harriet's outwardly devoted favorite, immediately suggests putting her in an institution and is exposed as having secretly married the woman Harriet once disapproved of while continuing to check on Harriet's fortune through her lawyer. Harriet reveals the bankruptcy was a ruse, reduces Roger to a five-dollar inheritance, welcomes Carol and Frank into her home, and agrees to become the financial 'angel' for Carol's play.

episodes.title: Two Notes (1946-03-13)
episodes.episodeDescription: Dr. Christian tells Judy about elderly neurologist Dr. Tuxbury, who has become convinced that his noisy upstairs tenant James Burton hates him and proudly describes what he believes is a perfect murder. Using a metronome and two repeated piano notes, Tuxbury claims he can exploit Burton's fear and heart response until the man's pulse races beyond endurance. The demonstration appears to work and Burton collapses, but the supposed victim has already recognized Tuxbury's growing paranoia and deliberately stages the reactions Tuxbury expects. No murder has taken place. Tuxbury is eventually confined to the state institution for the criminally insane, where he still reenacts his imaginary perfect crime for anyone willing to listen.

episodes.title: Man To Man (1946-03-20)
episodes.episodeDescription: Young Nicky Marshall, grieving the recent death of his father, asks Dr. Christian to marry his widowed mother because he longs for a little brother or sister and believes a new father is the only way that can happen. Dr. Christian gently explains that no one can replace the father Nicky's mother still loves, then widens the boy's idea of family by showing him how children of different backgrounds can live as brothers and sisters in one world. The conversation becomes unexpectedly personal when Nicky's mother telephones with news Dr. Christian has not yet known: she is already expecting another child by her late husband. Nicky leaves overjoyed that he will have the brother or sister he wanted without replacing the father he still loves.

episodes.title: The Vagabond Veteran (1946-03-27)
episodes.episodeDescription: Larry, a discharged fighter pilot, collapses in a Rivers End cafe convinced that recurring panic, suffocation and depression mean he is going insane. Dr. Christian recognizes a severe combat-nerves reaction rather than physical disease and brings Larry home instead of returning him to a hospital. Larry has no real home to return to, and the pressure and noise of a factory job after discharge only made his symptoms worse. Christian places him with the warm Santos family, where quiet routine and friendship with young Ted begin to restore him. A sudden startle in the garden makes Larry swing at Christian, terrifying him that he really is dangerous, but Christian refuses to give up on him. Later, while fishing with Christian and Ted, Christian falls into deep water. Larry reacts instantly, dives in and pulls him to safety without freezing or losing control. The emergency proves more convincingly than any reassurance that Larry's mind still functions under pressure. He accepts that he is recovering and agrees to stay with the Santos family, gaining the stable home and human connection he had been missing since the war.
