episodes.title: The Devil That Calls In The Night (1946-05-15)
episodes.displayTitle: The Devil That Calls In The Night (1946-05-15)
episodes.sortKey: 0|1946-05-15|00390|the devil that calls in the night 1946 05 15
episodes.episodeDescription: Young widow Margie is living in the old Blackwood house with her baby, little Jeffrey, and the domineering Lucinda when she begins hearing the voice of her dead husband Jeff calling to her at night. The unseen voice, mysterious objects and other frightening incidents steadily convince Margie that she is losing her mind. Dr. Christian is called after elderly servant Amos runs from the house in terror and collapses dead, insisting that a devil is loose inside. Remembering the houses old speaking-tube system, the doctor suspects a very human explanation. He has Tom imitate Jeffs voice through the tube, and Lucinda reacts in a way that exposes the scheme. She admits that she has been whispering to Margie and planting reminders of Jeff, first to frighten her into staying and later in hopes of driving her insane or to suicide so Lucinda could become guardian of the child. Dr. Christian removes Margie and the baby from the house, supports her future with Tom, and warns Lucinda that he will reveal the entire story, including the circumstances surrounding Amos death, if she tries to interfere.

episodes.title: Two Loves Had Marian (1946-07-03)
episodes.episodeDescription: Marian Douglas comes to Rivers End trying to find the soldier she remembers as David Rodell, a tall dark man she met at a New York servicemen's canteen and quickly fell in love with. Throughout the war she wrote to David Rodell overseas and fell even more deeply in love through his letters. When the real Rivers End David returned, however, he was shorter and blond, and Marian was so certain he was an impostor that she had him arrested for bothering her. Military records prove that the returning man is the genuine David and the man who actually received and answered Marian's wartime letters. Dr. Christian concludes that Marian has fused the real David's written personality with an idealized physical image formed around the stranger she first met. He recreates the emotional setting in which Marian originally fell in love, arranging a park encounter surrounded by butterflies. The memories finally join the real man to the feelings she already had for him. Marian recognizes David, the two marry the next morning, and Christian admits he helped the butterflies along with a little sugar water.

episodes.title: Spotlight On Grandma (1946-07-10)
episodes.episodeDescription: Grandma Benson has spent years raising her daughter's children and keeping the Forbes household running, but realizes that the family now notices her mainly when a blouse needs mending or some other chore is unfinished. Dr. Christian suggests that she finally take a vacation and let them discover how much they depend on her. Grandma goes considerably further: after hearing of a wealthy man's old sweetheart, Marie Monahan, she stages a supposed kidnapping and leaves a ransom note claiming she is the missing heiress and needs old love letters to prove it. Her frantic family suddenly listens to every story about her younger days and searches the house in panic. When Grandma returns safely, Dr. Christian reveals that he knew the heiress story could not be true. The kidnapping was Grandma's own theatrical way of turning the spotlight on a woman her family had taken for granted.

episodes.title: The Norton Nose (1947-09-17)
episodes.episodeDescription: A truck accident badly mangles young Pamela Norton's prominent family nose, and the reconstruction becomes a comic battle over identity. Pamela privately begs for a prettier nose, while formidable Aunt Augusta insists that the surgeon reproduce the ancestral Norton profile exactly from an old family miniature. Dr. Christian and the plastic surgeon refuse to turn Pamela into a museum piece and instead reconstruct a natural-looking nose suited to the young woman she actually is. The result helps free Pamela from years of embarrassment, and her romance with Mike Clancy moves toward marriage despite Augusta's outrage over the altered family landmark.

episodes.title: Cupids Boomerang (1947-11-26)
episodes.episodeDescription: Dr. Christian agrees to help the painfully shy Dan tell Sarah that he has loved her for years. At a charity dance the bachelor-club members tease the doctor into promising that he will make the proposal for Dan. The plan backfires spectacularly: when Dr. Christian tries to explain that someone wants Sarah as his wife, she assumes he means himself and accepts before he can correct her. With the town already congratulating them, the doctor cannot bring himself to humiliate Sarah by admitting the mistake, while Dan is crushed. Dr. Christian and his friends then stage a fake fire at Sarahs house with a homemade smoke bomb. Believing the house is burning, Dan rushes inside, carries Sarah out and finally blurts out his real feelings. Sarah admits that she loves Dan too and breaks her mistaken engagement to Dr. Christian, who pretends to take the rejection bravely. Once safely unengaged, he swears off matchmaking when another woman immediately tries to arrange yet another romantic introduction for him.

episodes.title: Sammy Hits The Jackpot (1949-07-13)
episodes.episodeDescription: Sammy La Coma, Riverâ€™s Endâ€™s irrepressible soda jerk, unexpectedly lands a logging contract and throws himself into the job despite everyoneâ€™s doubts about his experience. Working with capable logger Lucy, Sammy has to get a large shipment of logs to the river on schedule. A rival named Skilling repeatedly sabotages the operation, first damaging the road and later poisoning the crewâ€™s drinking water and tampering with a truck. Dr. Christian identifies the menâ€™s sudden illness as poisoning and helps keep the operation moving while Sammy catches Skilling at the truck and survives a rough fight with him. With drivers short and the deadline near, Dr. Christian and Lucy themselves help handle the heavy equipment so the last load reaches the river in time. Sammyâ€™s business gamble succeeds, but he considers the bigger jackpot to be Lucy, who kisses him after the final logs go in and then agrees to go to a movie with him.

episodes.title: Old Battle axe (1949-11-02)
episodes.episodeDescription: After forty years in the classroom and several serious heart attacks, strict teacher Sarah Adams, known to generations of Rivers End children as 'Old Battle Axe,' retires and insists she never wants to see another child. Needing an inexpensive place to live after leaving the school cottage, she rents a room from Bruce and Jane Crandall, whose five-year-old son David is blind. Sarah immediately begins ordering the household around, correcting grammar, rearranging routines and disciplining David, but beneath the severity she becomes deeply involved in the family's future. She pushes Bruce to seek more education, offers to look after the house and David while his parents work, and quietly forms a powerful attachment to the boy. Christian tells the family that David's clouded corneas might be replaced if suitable healthy corneas become available. A dying man, Sam Dennis, has offered his eyes, but Sarah condemns the idea as interfering with Providence. When Sam dies, his relatives refuse permission and the opportunity is lost. Sarah then suffers another grave attack and understands that she herself is dying. Before her death she makes Christian promise that David will receive her own corneas, formally arranging the gift so no relatives can block it. The woman who had objected to David seeing through another man's eyes ultimately chooses to let him see the world through hers, revealing the love hidden beneath the fearsome reputation of Rivers End's 'Old Battle Axe.'

episodes.title: Love Is A Two sided Thing (1950-10-04)
episodes.displayTitle: Love Is A Two sided Thing (1950-10-04)
episodes.episodeDescription: Newly elected county attorney Grant Newman reopens a manslaughter case against Earl Carlson, unaware that Earl is his wife Eileen's estranged brother. Eileen has hidden her poor background and family from Grant, and the deeper truth is worse: she, not Earl, was driving when an old man was struck, while Earl took the blame to protect her and Grant's political campaign. Dr. Christian finds an eyewitness who proves the death was an unavoidable accident, clearing the driver, but Grant's attempt to dismiss the case makes him look corrupt. Eileen publicly tells the truth to protect her husband from that suspicion, and the crisis forces both spouses to recognize that love and marriage cannot remain one-sided.

episodes.title: Dont Look Down (1950-10-25)
episodes.episodeDescription: While attending a medical meeting in New York, Dr. Christian is asked to help Joe Lance, a discouraged veteran who has reached a crisis after years of feeling trapped by a dull job, a troubled marriage and responsibility for his younger sister Audrey. Christian spends hours talking with Joe and gradually learns that beneath the despair he still wants the ordinary things he believes life has denied him: a real home, children, companionship and even simple pleasures such as fishing. Audrey's engagement removes one burden, but initially makes Joe feel even less needed. Christian refuses to deceive him and instead persuades the police to honor a promise allowing Joe time to reconsider. Joe finally comes back inside. His wife Emma, confronted with how selfish and distant their marriage has become, takes a risk of her own to reach him emotionally and promises that they will build the home and family he has wanted. Joe chooses to return with her. Audrey and Tim also prepare to marry, and Christian leaves New York with the family reconciled and looking forward rather than giving up.

episodes.title: The No Good (1950-11-29)
episodes.episodeDescription: The school board dismisses poor, troublesome teenager Lem Tolan as a no-good boy unworthy of a scholarship, but Dr. Christian sees intelligence and possibility beneath his record of mischief. When the family workhorse Noble breaks a leg and Lem becomes physically ill from fear that his father will shoot it, Dr. Christian realizes that the boy needs responsibility more than punishment. He arranges treatment for Noble and makes Lem responsible for the horse's difficult recovery, with the boy working off the expense at the doctor's office. Months of patient care transform Lem's behavior and prove his character, and the same scholarship committee finally agrees that he deserves the educational chance Dr. Christian wanted for him from the start.

episodes.title: The Other One (1951-02-21)
episodes.episodeDescription: Edward lies to police to protect his troubled brother Randolph, who is suspected in the death of schoolgirl Miriam Winslow. Dr. Christian patiently works past Edwards fierce family loyalty and uncovers a pattern of theft, secret spending and desperate attempts by Randolph to impress Miriam. Edward finally admits that Randolph met the girl wearing a hidden new jacket, tried to force an expensive necklace on her, and killed her when the encounter turned violent. Dr. Christian helps Edward understand that protecting his brother with lies will only deepen the damage, and that telling the truth is the only way to help both Randolph and their family.

episodes.title: The Runaway (1951-06-06)
episodes.episodeDescription: College basketball player Adam reaches Rivers End frightened and on the run. He finally admits to Dr. Christian that he helped fix games at Midwestern University and fled because he believes the gambling syndicate behind the scheme has sent two gangsters after him. From his hotel room he points out one man watching the elevator and another sitting across the street, convinced they are waiting to follow him onto a lonely road and kill him. Dr. Christian tells Adam that escape will only deepen his trouble and persuades him to return to school, confess the basketball fix and accept the consequences. To get him past the men he fears, the doctor smuggles him from the hotel on a covered ambulance stretcher and puts him aboard the train. Only afterward does Dr. Christian reveal the irony: the supposed gangsters are ordinary Rivers End fixtures, one a longtime hotel-lobby reader and the other a harmless man who spends his days reading on a park bench. Adams guilty conscience turned strangers into pursuers, but the fear still pushed him toward the honest decision he needed to make.

To get him past the men he fears, the doctor smuggles him from the hotel on a covered ambulance stretcher and puts him aboard the train. Only afterward does Dr. Christian reveal the irony: the supposed gangsters are ordinary Rivers End fixtures, one a longtime hotel-lobby reader and the other a harmless man who spends his days reading on a park bench. Adams guilty conscience turned strangers into pursuers, but the fear still pushed him toward the honest decision he needed to make.

episodes.title: Corresponding Corpse (date unknown)
episodes.episodeDescription: A Havana businessman hires Shayne after receiving an urgent letter from his friend Julian, even though everyone in New Orleans insists Julian died two years earlier. Shayne uncovers a blackmail scheme involving Julian's old organization and a forger imitating the dead man's handwriting, while the client himself admits he killed the real Julian years before. This undated 27-minute recording is preserved separately because catalog and acoustic review show it is a distinct surviving version rather than the December 16 master.

episodes.title: Number 13 (1950-03-06)
episodes.episodeDescription: Randy Stone is held up by an elderly former professor, then discovers the man is trying to prove a roulette system with borrowed money. The system builds a fortune, but after the professor dies his wife carries out one final promised bet and loses it all when the wheel lands on number 13, ending the obsession that had consumed him.

episodes.title: Old Blind Pop (1950-08-07)
episodes.episodeDescription: Randy befriends a blind street musician who has spent years avoiding his daughter Vicki while pretending he is still successful. Vicki has been writing home with a lie of her own, claiming a glamorous ballet career, and Randy brings father and daughter together so both can finally admit the truth and discover that neither failure nor disability has changed their love for each other.

episodes.title: Gunner's Last Fight (1950-08-14)
episodes.episodeDescription: Randy tries to help boxer Gunner Evans after gamblers rough him up for refusing to throw a fight. The pressure becomes more dangerous when Randy discovers that Gunner's own wife is working with the men trying to control the bout.

episodes.title: Doctor's Secret (1950-08-21)
episodes.episodeDescription: Sent to Joliet to cover an execution, Randy meets Dr. Graham, an alcoholic physician whose son is about to die in the electric chair. Graham's tortured behavior convinces Randy that the doctor carries a deeper guilt connected to the crime, and Randy pushes toward the secret before the execution becomes irreversible.

episodes.title: Old Home Week (1950-09-04)
episodes.episodeDescription: On a short vacation at Paradise Lake, Randy rescues Pat Torrance from the water and immediately suspects there is more to her apparent drowning. His attempt to sort out what happened puts him in the middle of a bitter tangle involving a husband, an ex-wife and former girlfriends with motives of their own.

episodes.title: The Hunter Becomes the Hunted (1950-09-11)
episodes.episodeDescription: Escaped condemned prisoner John Galt kidnaps Randy and the district attorney who prosecuted him, insisting that he was wrongly convicted. Rather than simply fleeing, Galt forces the two men into his desperate attempt to uncover the evidence he believes can prove his innocence before the law catches up with him again.

episodes.episodeDescription: A frightened young woman named Mary Callahan offers Randy information about the murder of notorious gambler Marty Crain, but demands five hundred dollars for the story. Randy refuses to buy news, then follows her lead anyway and uncovers the hatred, revenge and manipulation behind both the murder and Mary's attempt to sell its secret.

episodes.episodeDescription: On a rainy night Randy investigates the killing of Nick Corby in a rundown neighborhood where suspicion quickly centers on a strange black cat and the eccentric people around it. Randy uncovers blackmail, loyalty and family secrets, then decides that telling the whole story in print would hurt innocent people more than it would serve the truth.

episodes.episodeDescription: Five-year-old Jody Letterin is taken into a church bell tower by a frightened man who threatens to kill him if police close in. Randy realizes that the crowd, searchlights and armed response are feeding the man's need for attention, and argues that giving him true sanctuary may be the safest way to bring the child down alive.

episodes.episodeDescription: Randy becomes involved with a gravely ill woman who is determined to find her missing husband before she dies. Her search for Antonio leads Randy through old relationships and unanswered questions about why the man vanished and whether he can still be brought back to her in time.

episodes.title: Lost Souls (1951-11-16)

As Randy protects her and tests whether anyone is really pursuing her, the haunting is traced to unresolved guilt and trauma from Ruth's childhood, giving her a chance to seek help instead of continuing to run.

episodes.episodeDescription: Randy gets caught up in the nerves of expectant father Ben Troy while Ben's wife is about to have their baby. Ben becomes so frantic over the birth that Randy winds up managing the anxious husband almost as much as the real medical emergency.

episodes.episodeDescription: Randy investigates the claim of a convicted murderer who insists that the killing for which he was blamed was actually committed by Gusher James, a wealthy and influential oil man. The accusation sends Randy against money and power as he tries to determine whether the prisoner's story is a last desperate lie or the truth.

Ben fears his reckless younger brother's return to racing, while Keeney believes Ben is trying to protect his own fading career, and the conflict drives the brothers toward a dangerous reckoning on the racetrack.

episodes.episodeDescription: Benjamin Tusher, a farmer from rural Illinois, arrives in Chicago determined to reform a corrupt political machine without violence. Randy watches Tusher confront the city's entrenched interests with an almost disarming belief in goodwill and love, and discovers that the simple approach is more effective than anyone expects.

episodes.episodeDescription: Randy notices that veteran printer Dutch Hildebrand has deliberately removed part of reporter Gil Lovett's story before publication. episodes.episodeDescription: A call to the Chicago Star warns that a bomb is aboard an airliner. Randy cannot dismiss it as a crank call, so he races to protect the passengers and identify who planted the explosive before the threatened flight ends in disaster.

episodes.episodeDescription: Randy investigates young dancer Larry Wilson after a racketeer becomes determined to buy his services and Larry abruptly walks away from a promising theatrical break. The mystery ends at a rectory, where Randy learns Larry has chosen a different calling entirely: he is leaving show business to enter the seminary and become a priest.

episodes.episodeDescription: Randy investigates after Brother James, the organist at a Skid Row mission, is beaten and someone throws a hand grenade into the mission. The violence points toward a policy gambling racket and forces Randy to uncover why a charitable refuge has become a target.

episodes.episodeDescription: A mentally disturbed killer admits murdering three women but insists he did not commit a fourth similar slaying. Randy takes the denial seriously and investigates whether the latest victim belongs to a different crime hidden behind the earlier murders.

episodes.title: Stagecoach (1949-01-09)
episodes.episodeDescription: A mixed group of passengers crosses dangerous Arizona country by stagecoach while Geronimo's Apaches threaten the route. Fugitive Ringo Kid joins the coach and falls for Dallas, an ostracized young woman who understands his loneliness, while the passengers survive a birth, an Apache attack and a last-minute cavalry rescue. In Lordsburg Ringo insists on facing the Plummer brothers who killed his family. He survives the showdown, and Luke Plummer's dying confession clears Ringo, leaving him free to leave with Dallas and begin the life they imagined together.

episodes.episodeDescription: Overworked advertising executive Duke Crawford is so frayed by a demanding cosmetics client and former fiancÃ©e, Michelle Bennett, that he hears phantom telephones and declares he hates women. His boss gives him a self-help book, Letâ€™s Live a Little, and Duke promptly turns its author, neurologist Dr. Jo Loring, into both his doctor and a publicity account. episodes.title: The Exile (1949-01-23)
episodes.episodeDescription: With England ruled by Cromwell, the future Charles II lives in exile in Holland, hiding his identity while loyal supporters wait for a chance to restore him. During his wandering he finds shelter and work with Katie, whose practical life at her inn and farm offers him a peace far removed from courts and civil war, and the two fall in love. Charles is eventually drawn back into the royal cause when supporters and enemies converge on his refuge, forcing him to fight for both his life and his claim. After the immediate danger is defeated, word arrives that a new free Parliament has invited him to return to England as king on terms that include the freedoms he demanded. Katie knows he belongs to his people rather than to her alone, and they part with a final promise of enduring love as Charles leaves to reclaim the throne.

episodes.title: Mr and Mrs Smith (1949-01-30)
episodes.episodeDescription: David and Ann Smith learn that a legal technicality means their three-year marriage was never valid. David assumes they will simply marry again, but Ann is furious when he treats the situation casually and decides to make him earn her back. She begins seeing David's law partner Jefferson, whose courtly Southern manners give David a very real rival. The contest follows them to a winter resort, where Ann stages one last attempt to make David give up on her and David refuses to be driven away. Their jealousy finally exposes that neither wants anyone else, and the Smiths reconcile as a couple all over again.

episodes.title: Hired Wife (1949-02-06)
episodes.episodeDescription: Efficient secretary Kendall Browning secretly loves her boss, cement-company owner Stephen Dexter, but spends every spring watching him fall for another glamorous woman. When a rival company threatens to tie up every asset Stephen owns, his lawyer proposes a temporary marriage so the business can be transferred into a wife's name until the legal danger passes. Stephen wants model Phyllis Walden, but Kendall's attempt to arrange that marriage goes wrong and she ends up becoming Stephen's legal wife herself. Once Kendall controls the company she stops behaving like a compliant secretary, and the resulting battle finally makes Stephen see her as the woman she has always been. Their business marriage becomes real, and Stephen asks her to marry him just before remembering that they already are.

episodes.title: Magnificent Obsession (1949-02-13)
episodes.episodeDescription: Reckless millionaire Robert Merrick nearly drowns, and the emergency equipment used to save him is therefore unavailable when beloved physician Dr. Hudson suffers a fatal accident. Hudsonâ€™s widow Helen resents Robert for the loss, and Robertâ€™s careless attempt to force a reconciliation contributes to another accident that leaves her blind. Haunted by the damage he has caused, Robert embraces the late doctorâ€™s ideal of quietly helping others, returns to medicine, and falls deeply in love with Helen. In Paris she learns his identity but also recognizes the man he has become; fearing that marriage to a blind woman would burden him, she leaves. Six years later Robert returns as a physician, performs the difficult operation himself, and Helen opens her eyes to light, with the promise that her sight will continue to return.

episodes.title: The Prisoner of Zenda (1949-02-20)
episodes.episodeDescription: Englishman Rudolf Rassendyll arrives in Ruritania and, because he is nearly identical to King Rudolf, is forced to impersonate the monarch after the king is drugged and kidnapped by the ambitious Black Michael. While carrying the deception through court and falling in love with Princess Flavia, Rassendyll learns the real king is imprisoned at Zenda Castle. He helps rescue the king and defeats the plot, then gives up both the throne and Flavia because her duty is to her country and its rightful ruler.

When a vision convinces him that staying with Jenny will lead to her death, he disappears; Jenny later marries Courtland and dies after giving birth to their daughter Jean. Triton intervenes, saves her, and dies beside a marble lion, fulfilling the final vision he had already recorded in his diary.

episodes.title: A Foreign Affair (1949-03-06)
episodes.episodeDescription: Congresswoman Phoebe Frost arrives in occupied Berlin to investigate the conduct of American troops and quickly focuses on nightclub singer Erika von Schlütow, a former Nazi whose protection appears to reach inside the U.S. Army. Captain John Pringle is secretly involved with Erika and tries to divert Phoebe by romancing her, only to find his feelings becoming real. The investigation and love triangle collide as Erika's past is exposed, leaving Pringle and Phoebe to confront what began as deception and turned into a genuine affair.

episodes.title: You Were Meant for Me (1949-03-13)
episodes.episodeDescription: Bandleader Chuck Arnold meets small-town Peggy Mayhew during the last glittering months of the 1920s, and after a missed rendezvous and one decisive kiss he proposes. Peggy joins Chuck on the road as his orchestra climbs toward a New York booking, but the 1929 market crash wipes out Chuckâ€™s savings and collapses the touring business around him. The couple retreats to Peggyâ€™s family home in Bloomington, where Chuckâ€™s pride makes unemployment harder to bear than poverty itself. episodes.title: The Perfect Marriage (1949-03-20)
episodes.episodeDescription: On their fifth anniversary, successful husband and wife Dale and Jenny Williams realize that their supposedly perfect marriage has gone flat and that familiarity has replaced romance. Talk of separation becomes serious when old flames Gloria and Gil reappear, giving each spouse reason to suspect the other has already moved on. The jealousy they thought had vanished returns with force, and both discover that they still care far more than they admitted. After comic attempts to provoke one another collapse, Dale and Jenny shut out their would-be alternatives, celebrate their anniversary after all, and rediscover the marriage they nearly abandoned.

episodes.title: Suddenly Its Spring (1949-03-27)
episodes.episodeDescription: Husband-and-wife lawyers Peter and Mary Morley return from wartime service after years apart only to discover that distance, pride and unspoken hurt have left their marriage close to divorce. Mary wants Peter to sign a divorce consent, while Peter realizes that he still loves her and tries a series of increasingly foolish schemes to make himself repulsive enough that she will decide against leaving him for another man. Their games produce jealousy, public embarrassment and competing romantic plans, but eventually Peter signs the papers because he believes Mary truly wants her freedom. As they divide the possessions in their apartment, each old object brings back a memory and exposes the misunderstandings they never discussed, including their grief over not having a child and the possibility that they could have adopted. A broken music box begins playing after being shaken, giving them an obvious metaphor for their own marriage. Mary finally dismisses the other man, and she and Peter abandon the divorce and reconcile.

episodes.title: The Ghost Breakers (1949-04-03)
episodes.episodeDescription: Radio personality Larry Lawrence becomes entangled with Mary Carter and follows her to a supposedly haunted castle on a Cuban island she has inherited. Ghostly warnings, a zombie, secret passages and murder threats seem to confirm the island's curse, but Larry keeps discovering very human motives behind the scares. The real prize is a rich silver deposit, and Montgomery and his partners have been using the supernatural legend to frighten Mary away and keep control of it. Their conspiracy collapses in a gunfight with police, leaving Mary wealthy and Larry insisting that the ghosts were tricks, just before one final unexplained scare undercuts his certainty.

episodes.title: Music for Millions (1949-04-10)
episodes.episodeDescription: Young Mike comes to New York to live with her older sister Barbara, a bassist in a women's symphony orchestra who is pregnant while her husband Joe serves overseas. When a telegram reports Joe missing and presumed dead, Barbara's friends hide the news until after the baby is born, even arranging a forged letter that appears to come from Joe so she will keep hoping. The deception nearly collapses when Barbara realizes something is wrong, but after the birth a genuine letter arrives: Joe survived months stranded after parachuting from a plane and is alive. With both Joe and the newborn safe, the orchestra changes its program to the Hallelujah Chorus in celebration.

episodes.title: The Best Years of Our Lives (1949-04-17)
episodes.displayTitle: The Best Years of Our Lives (1949-04-17)
episodes.episodeDescription: Bombardier Fred Derry, banker Al Stevenson, and Navy veteran Homer Parrish return together to Boone City after the war, each discovering that home is no longer as simple as memory made it. Homer, who lost both hands, fears that his devoted fiancÃ©e Wilma will eventually regret marrying a disabled man. Al returns to his family and banking career carrying the emotional dislocation of combat, while Fred finds that his wartime rank means little in civilian life and that his marriage to Marie cannot survive his unemployment and changed outlook. Fred and Alâ€™s daughter Peggy fall in love, but Al insists Fred end the relationship while he is still married. After Fred loses his drugstore job defending Homer and other veterans, he pushes Homer to trust Wilma rather than sacrifice their future out of fear. At Homer and Wilmaâ€™s wedding, Fred reveals that Marie is divorcing him and that he has found new work. Peggy accepts the difficult life ahead, and Fred realizes the best years of his life may still be in front of him.

episodes.title: The Skys the Limit (1949-04-24)
episodes.episodeDescription: Decorated fighter pilot Jerry Burton comes home on leave and, tired of being treated as a public hero, hides his identity while enjoying New York as an ordinary man. He falls for magazine photographer Jean, but his evasiveness and apparently aimless behavior make her believe he is wasting his life while editor Phil also hopes to marry her. Jerry cannot tell her that his leave is ending and that he is returning to combat. Phil sends Jean to photograph departing fighter pilots, and at the airfield she finally discovers who Jerry really is. They confess their love just before his transport takes off, with Jean promising to wait for him until the war is over.

episodes.title: The Trouble with Women (1949-05-01)
episodes.episodeDescription: Reporter Kate Farrell writes a sensational article about psychology professor Gilbert Sedley that leaves her newspaper facing a major libel suit, including the claim that he believes in hitting women. To manufacture proof, Kate enrolls in Sedley's class under cover and repeatedly tries to provoke him into striking her. Instead the combative experiment turns into romance, and the escalating deception finally spills into court, where psychology, hypnosis and Kate's real feelings undo the scandal she set out to create.

episodes.title: Its a Wonderful Life (1949-05-08)
episodes.episodeDescription: George Bailey has spent his life sacrificing his own ambitions to help the people of Bedford Falls through the family building-and-loan. On Christmas Eve, an $8,000 shortage leaves him facing disgrace and possible arrest, and in despair he wishes he had never been born. Clarence, an angel hoping to earn his wings, grants that wish and shows George a grim alternate Bedford Falls in which his brother died young, his mother does not know him, Mary never married, and many people George once helped were left far worse off. Realizing how deeply his life is woven into the lives of others, George begs to live again. Restored to his family, he learns that the townspeople he helped for years have raised more than enough money to cover the loss, and the sound of Christmas chimes tells him Clarence has earned his wings.

episodes.title: Hold Back the Dawn (1949-05-15)
episodes.episodeDescription: Romanian confidence man and former gigolo Georges Iscovescu is stranded in Mexico waiting years for an immigration quota number that will let him enter the United States. When an old acquaintance explains that marriage to an American offers a quicker route across the border, Georges sets his sights on Emmy Brown, a trusting American schoolteacher whose station wagon has broken down nearby. He marries Emmy intending only to use her for immigration, while Anita, another woman from his past, waits for him to complete the scheme. During a honeymoon trip Georges unexpectedly falls genuinely in love with his wife. Anita later tells Emmy the truth about the wedding and Georgesâ€™s past, and a devastated Emmy leaves. When Georges has a sudden vision that she has been hurt in an automobile accident, he crashes the border to reach her hospital bedside, sacrificing his chance of legal entry. His devotion restores Emmyâ€™s will to live, and the immigration inspector who followed him chooses not to report the crossing, leaving Georges and Emmy together as a real husband and wife.

episodes.title: Her Husbands Affair (1949-05-22)
episodes.episodeDescription: Margaret Weldon loves her ambitious husband Bill, but his confidence repeatedly outruns his judgment, especially when he throws himself into the inventions of an eccentric professor. A new cream is promoted as a hair remover, only to produce the opposite result and leave its test subjects sprouting alarming amounts of hair. With lawsuits and the governor furious, Margaret recognizes that the failed remover is actually a potentially valuable hair restorer and turns the disaster into a commercial opportunity. Bill resents her habit of rescuing his schemes and makes her promise to stop interfering, but almost immediately the professor arrives with another accidental invention, a fluid that preserves flowers indefinitely. Bill forgets every lesson he has just learned and eagerly launches the next venture with Margaret at his side.

episodes.title: Trade Winds (1949-05-29)
episodes.episodeDescription: Private detective Sam Wye is sent across the Pacific to bring back fugitive Kay Kerrigan, who believes she murdered playboy Tommy Broome after he drove her sister to suicide. Sam falls for Kay and spots a crucial contradiction: Kay remembers shooting Broome in the heart, but he died from a bullet to the head, and a pair of black antelope gloves at the scene were not hers. Sam gathers the women linked to Broome and uses the gloves as bait; Mrs. Cornell claims them and finally admits that Kay's gun held blanks and that her husband Walden killed Broome after Kay left. With the confession secretly witnessed, Kay is cleared and Sam's pursuit ends in marriage rather than arrest.

episodes.title: The Killers (1949-06-05)
episodes.episodeDescription: When hitmen murder former boxer Swede Anderson without resistance, the investigation works backward through his life to explain why he simply waited for death. Swede had fallen in with Big Jim Colfax's gang, joined a major robbery, double-crossed the others for the stolen money and fled with Kitty, only to be betrayed and stripped of the cash himself. Years later the old crime catches up with him, leaving Swede convinced there is nowhere left to run.

episodes.displayTitle: Mr Blandings Builds His Dream House (1949-07-01)
episodes.episodeDescription: Advertising executive Jim Blandings is tired of cramped New York apartment life and decides that moving his family to the country will solve everything. Jimâ€™s work suffers at the same time because he cannot find a slogan for the Wham ham account, while his friend Billâ€™s constant helpfulness around Muriel gives Jim one more thing to worry about. episodes.title: The Big Clock (1949-07-08)
episodes.episodeDescription: George Stroud works inside the vast Janoth publishing organization, where his domineering boss has built an empire ruled by schedules, deadlines, and the enormous clock in the company lobby. After Janoth kills Pauline York, the woman Stroud had also been seeing, Stroud discovers that the unidentified man the company has ordered him to hunt is himself. Forced to direct the investigation, he uses the companyâ€™s own research machinery while desperately keeping his identity hidden and gathering evidence against Janoth. Janoth tries to flee, falls into the buildingâ€™s generator machinery, and is electrocuted, ending both the murder hunt and his obsessive control of the clock.

episodes.title: Yellow Sky (1949-07-15)
episodes.episodeDescription: After a bank robbery, outlaw leader Stretch and his exhausted gang cross a deadly desert and reach the abandoned mining town of Yellow Sky. There they find only an old prospector and his fiercely independent granddaughter Mike, who are secretly working a rich gold claim. The gang quickly turns on its hosts and on itself over the treasure, while Stretch, increasingly drawn to Mike, tries to keep the others from simply taking everything. Greed splits the outlaws into rival factions, and Dude and Lengthy move to seize the gold for themselves. Stretch survives the final gunfight, returns his gun to Mike, and declares that he is through with the life that brought him there. With the dangerous members of the gang gone, he asks Mike and her grandfather to let him remain in Yellow Sky.

episodes.title: Casbah (1949-07-22)
episodes.episodeDescription: Master thief Pepe le Moko is safe from arrest only while he remains inside the maze of Algiers' Casbah. His love for visiting Gaby gives Inspector Slimane the weakness he has been waiting for: Slimane falsely tells Gaby that Pepe is dead and arranges her departure, knowing Pepe will leave the Casbah to reach her. Pepe walks into the trap at the airport as Gaby's plane leaves for Paris, losing the sanctuary that had kept him beyond the law.

episodes.title: Saigon (1949-07-29)
episodes.episodeDescription: After the war, pilot Larry Briggs learns that his badly wounded friend Mike Perry has only a few months to live. Larry and Pete Rocco decide not to tell Mike and instead take a lucrative flying job in the Orient so they can fill his remaining time with adventure. Their employer, Alex Maris, turns out to be a wanted war profiteer, and his secretary Susan Cleaver is carrying a briefcase containing roughly half a million dollars. Mike falls for Susan while Larry distrusts her, then Larry seizes the money and tries to force her away from Mike before the scheme destroys him. The groupâ€™s flight into Indochina draws police attention, Maris catches up with them, and the criminal plot collapses in violence. Pete is killed, Mike dies from his condition, and Maris is shot. With the money recovered and the police satisfied, Larry and Susan leave Saigon together, both chastened by the lives lost around them.

episodes.title: Fort Apache (1949-08-05)
episodes.episodeDescription: At remote Fort Apache, experienced Captain Kirby York understands that Cochise and his people have left the reservation because corrupt Indian agent Meacham has cheated and abused them. York risks an unarmed mission into Apache country and persuades Cochise to return for peace talks after promising fair treatment. The fortâ€™s rigid commander, Colonel Thursday, ignores both Yorkâ€™s warning and Cochiseâ€™s grievances, treats negotiation as humiliation, and orders the Apache back under Meachamâ€™s authority. Thursday then dismisses Yorkâ€™s warning of an ambush and leads the regiment into a narrow pass, where nearly the entire command is destroyed. Wounded, Thursday refuses rescue and dies with his men. When Cochise approaches the remaining wagons, York keeps his promise and meets him unarmed; Cochise returns the regimental flag. The regiment is later rebuilt, carrying forward the names and memory of the men who died.

episodes.title: Jezebel (1949-08-12)
episodes.episodeDescription: Proud New Orleans belle Julie Marsden repeatedly tests and humiliates her fiancé Pres Dillard until her defiance destroys their engagement. When Pres later returns married to Amy, Julie tries to reclaim him and provokes jealous rivalries that end in a fatal duel. A yellow-fever epidemic then strikes New Orleans and Pres falls gravely ill. Realizing the damage her selfishness has caused, Julie asks Amy to let her accompany Pres to the deadly quarantine island because she knows the local conditions and can fight for his survival. Amy agrees, giving Julie a final chance at redemption through sacrifice rather than possession.

episodes.title: Love Crazy (1949-08-19)
episodes.episodeDescription: Steve and Susan Ireland expect to celebrate their wedding anniversary quietly, but a meddling mother-in-law and a series of innocent-looking encounters with another woman convince Susan that Steve is unfaithful. When she pushes ahead with a divorce, Steve seizes on a lawyerâ€™s suggestion that a legally insane husband cannot be divorced immediately and begins pretending to be mad. The scheme becomes much less funny when doctors actually declare him insane and place him under Susanâ€™s custody, forcing Steve into increasingly frantic attempts to escape and explain himself. A jammed elevator finally brings Steve, Susan, and the other woman together long enough for the truth to come out. Susan realizes the supposed affair was innocent, her anger collapses, and the two reconcile instead of divorcing.

episodes.title: Appointment for Love (1949-08-26)
episodes.episodeDescription: Successful playwright Andre marries independent doctor Jane, only to discover that she intends marriage to preserve two separate people rather than merge them into one household. She takes an apartment several floors above his so each can continue working and living independently, leaving Andre baffled and increasingly jealous. Both begin manipulating appearances and outside admirers to prove that jealousy really does matter, turning the apartment building into a comic battlefield. After the games finally expose how much they actually want each other, the pair abandon their experiment in detached marriage and reconcile.

episodes.title: Apartment for Peggy (1949-09-02)
episodes.episodeDescription: Retired professor Henry Barnes, convinced that age has made him useless, rents his attic to veteran student Jason Taylor and Jason's energetic pregnant wife Peggy during the postwar housing shortage. Peggy draws Barnes back into life, persuading him to organize classes for veterans' wives and reminding him that knowledge matters only when it helps people. After Peggy loses her baby, guilt and financial pressure drive Jason to abandon school for a better-paying sales job, and Peggy prepares to leave as well. Believing he has lost the people who gave him purpose, Barnes takes what he thinks are sleeping pills, only for Peggy and the returning Jason to discover the tablets were harmless. Jason chooses teaching again, Peggy stays, and Barnes realizes he is needed after all.

episodes.title: The Human Comedy (1949-09-09)
episodes.episodeDescription: Teenager Homer Macauley works as a bicycle messenger in wartime Ithaca, carrying the small joys and devastating news of his neighbors while his older brother Marcus serves overseas. Through school, family and the telegraph office, Homer learns that becoming a man means recognizing both difference and shared humanity. Elderly telegrapher Willie Grogan dies at his desk just as the message arrives that Marcus has been killed in the war. Before Homer can bring the telegram home, Marcus's wounded Army friend Tobey arrives in Ithaca, saying Marcus made him part of the family. Homer tears up the death notice and welcomes Tobey into the Macauley home as the living piece of his brother that has returned.

episodes.title: Whispering Smith (1949-09-16)
episodes.episodeDescription: Railroad detective Luke 'Whispering' Smith returns to Medicine Bend and discovers that his old friend Murray Sinclair has crossed from questionable salvage into organized theft, sabotage and train robbery with Rebstock's gang. Smith tries to pull Murray back for the sake of the woman they both care about, but Murray kills Rebstock, turns on Smith and refuses every chance to surrender. Their friendship ends in a final armed confrontation in which Smith is forced to shoot the dying Murray after Murray draws on him one last time.

episodes.title: Dont Trust Your Husband (1949-09-23)
episodes.episodeDescription: Advertising man Vince repeatedly comes home late claiming business with a mysterious Mr. Frazier, only for his wife Paula to discover that Frazier is a woman and suspect an affair. Trying to prove that jealousy works both ways, Vince encourages handsome stranger Claude Kimball to flirt with Paula, not realizing Kimball is a wealthy tobacco executive who begins taking the assignment seriously. The scheme escalates into threats of divorce, competing romances and a badly timed confession until the real business client appears and the manufactured jealousy collapses. After one final comic misunderstanding with a hired admirer, Vince and Paula reconcile.

episodes.title: Pride of the Yankees (1949-09-30)
episodes.episodeDescription: The story follows Lou Gehrig from a powerful Columbia ballplayer into a Yankees rookie, his romance and marriage with Eleanor, and the long run of durability that earns him the name the Iron Man. As his consecutive-game record and fame grow, unexplained weakness finally forces him from the lineup and doctors diagnose the fatal illness that will bear his name. At Yankee Stadium, surrounded by teammates and fans, Gehrig refuses self-pity and calls himself the luckiest man on the face of the earth before walking away from baseball to a final ovation.

episodes.title: The Senator Was Indiscreet (1949-10-03)
episodes.episodeDescription: Vain but spectacularly inept Senator Melvin G. Ashton decides that his growing publicity proves the country wants him for president, while his press agent Luke Gibson struggles to contain the damage and marry sharp-tongued columnist Poppy McNaughton. As Ashton's accidental popularity grows, everyone around him worries about the private diary in which he has recorded years of political secrets and indiscretions. Poppy finally gets hold of the diary and sends it toward the newspapers just as Ashton convinces himself the White House is within reach. Realizing publication will destroy him, the senator abruptly abandons the presidential campaign and starts dreaming instead of being summoned to lead somewhere as remote as Outer Mongolia.

episodes.title: Criss Cross (1949-10-10)
episodes.episodeDescription: Armored-truck driver Steve Thompson cannot let go of his former lover Anna, even after she marries gangster Slim Dundee. When Slim discovers them together, Steve invents an armored-car robbery to explain the meeting and secretly plans to use the heist to escape with Anna. The robbery kills an old guard and leaves Steve wounded, while Slim survives and sends gunman Vincent to finish him. Steve bribes Vincent to take him to Anna, only to discover that her promises were driven by money and self-preservation. Slim arrives at the hideout as Anna turns back to Steve for protection, and the final confrontation ends in gunfire just as police close in. Steveâ€™s detective friend Pete can only tell him that Anna was poison and that some men have to learn the truth the hard way.

episodes.title: Pitfall (1949-10-17)
episodes.episodeDescription: Insurance investigator John Forbes is bored with the routine of suburban marriage when his work brings him to Mona Stevens, who received expensive gifts bought with money embezzled by her imprisoned boyfriend. John should simply recover the property, but attraction leads to a brief affair that he hides from his wife Sue. Private detective MacDonald, already obsessed with Mona, discovers the relationship and begins threatening both John and Mona. After the embezzler is released, the jealous and increasingly violent chain of events reaches Johnâ€™s home, where John kills the armed man in self-defense while Mona shoots MacDonald. John finally tells the police and then Sue the whole truth. Sue considers leaving him but decides that one terrible lapse should not automatically erase an otherwise good marriage, and the couple agree to try to rebuild what his deception damaged.

episodes.title: Love Letters (1949-10-24)
episodes.episodeDescription: During the war, Captain Alan Quinton writes deeply personal love letters for his less articulate friend Roger Morland to a young woman named Victoria. Alan falls in love with the unseen recipient through his own words, but Roger returns home, marries Victoria, and later tells her that the letters were never his. After Roger is found stabbed to death, Alan comes home convinced that Victoria killed him and eventually meets an amnesiac young woman known as Singleton, not realizing she is Victoria herself. The two fall in love while Alan struggles with the knowledge of her past. Returning to Meadow Farm finally restores the missing truth: Victoriaâ€™s guardian, Beatrice Remington, killed Roger after he struck Victoria, and Victoriaâ€™s shock erased her memory. Cleared of the murder and reunited with the man who truly wrote the letters she loved, Victoria and Alan can finally claim the relationship that began before they ever met.

episodes.title: Remember the Night (1949-10-31)
episodes.episodeDescription: Lee Leander is arrested for stealing a diamond bracelet just before Christmas, and prosecutor John Sargent has the case postponed until after the holidays rather than risk a sympathetic jury. Feeling responsible for leaving her jailed over Christmas, John arranges bail and discovers that Lee has nowhere worth returning to, so he takes her along to his own family home. The warmth of Johnâ€™s mother and aunt gives Lee a glimpse of the honest life she never had, and she and John fall in love on the trip back to New York. At trial John quietly tries to give her every possible chance, but Lee refuses to let his love compromise his duty. She pleads guilty, accepting that she must pay for what she did. John promises to stand beside her through sentencing and whatever prison term follows, while Lee hopes that if he still wants her afterward they can begin together on equal terms.

episodes.title: Body and Soul (1949-11-11)
episodes.episodeDescription: Charlie Davis rises from neighborhood boxer to champion, but success ties him to promoter Roberts and a corrupt fight business that treats fighters as disposable assets. After an opponent with a known brain injury dies following a rigged bout, Charlie finally understands the human cost of the racket, even as Roberts arranges for him to throw his own title fight. Given $60,000 to bet against himself, Charlie instead fights to win, rejecting the fix and Roberts' control. He leaves the ring bruised but morally free, reunited with Peg and declaring that Roberts can no longer take anything from him.

episodes.title: The Uninvited (1949-11-18)
episodes.episodeDescription: Rick Fitzgerald and his sister Pamela buy an old seaside house despite its reputation for ghostly sobbing and unexplained cold. The mystery deepens when young Stella Meredith, whose mother supposedly died falling from the nearby cliff, is drawn compulsively to the house and nearly goes over the same precipice. Rick investigates the old Meredith household and learns of Mary Meredith, her husbandâ€™s Spanish model Carmel, and a long-buried scandal. The accepted story says Carmel was the dangerous rival, but the hauntings reveal the opposite truth: Stella is actually Carmelâ€™s daughter, and Mary Meredith was the jealous woman who tried to kill the child and died at the cliff. Carmelâ€™s spirit finally reaches Stella with love and peace, while Rick confronts the malevolent apparition of Mary and drives it from the house, ending the haunting and freeing Stella from the false history of her birth.

episodes.title: Spiral Staircase (1949-11-25)
episodes.episodeDescription: Traumatized by witnessing her parents' deaths, Helen has been unable to speak for years and works in the Warren household while a killer stalks women he considers physically imperfect. During a storm, suspicion seems to point toward volatile Steven Warren, but Helen discovers that the apparently respectable professor is the murderer and that he has deliberately used Steven's presence to divert suspicion. Trapped in the house and targeted because of her muteness, Helen races up and down the spiral staircase trying to reach Mrs. Warren's gun. Mrs. Warren finally shoots the killer, and the shock breaks Helen's silence: she is able to telephone Dr. Perry herself and speak for the first time since childhood.

episodes.title: All My Sons (1949-12-02)
episodes.episodeDescription: Manufacturer Joe Keller has built his life around providing for his family, but his son Chris discovers that Joe knowingly allowed defective aircraft cylinders to be shipped during the war and let partner Herbert Deever take the blame. Twenty-one pilots died, and Joe insists he did it to protect the business for his sons. A letter from missing son Larry reveals that Larry learned of his father's crime and deliberately went to his death because he could not live with the shame. Joe finally understands that the dead airmen were 'all my sons' too. Moments later a gunshot from the house tells Chris that his father has killed himself.

episodes.title: Call Northside 777 (1949-12-09)
episodes.episodeDescription: Chicago reporter McNeil reopens the case of Frank Wiecek, imprisoned for the murder of a policeman after an identification by speakeasy owner Wanda Skutnik. What begins as a human-interest story driven by Frank's mother's long campaign becomes a search for evidence that the conviction was wrong. McNeil finally finds a newspaper photograph showing Skutnik with Frank before the date she swore she first saw him; an enlargement reveals the date on a newsboy's paper as December 22. The proof establishes perjured identification testimony and wins Frank his freedom after years in prison.

episodes.title: The Affairs of Susan (1949-12-16)
episodes.episodeDescription: Susan's prospective husband tries to understand the woman he plans to marry by questioning the men who knew her before him. Ex-husband Roger remembers an innocent country girl, writer Bill recalls an intellectual companion, and Westerner Mike describes an adventurous outdoor woman, leaving the fiancé wondering which Susan is real. The answer is that each man saw the side of her that his own expectations brought out. After the newer suitors step aside, Roger returns and admits that he was too impatient to understand the young woman he married. Susan realizes she still loves him, and the divorced couple reunites.

episodes.title: Miracle on 34th Street (1949-12-23)
episodes.episodeDescription: Macy's hires kindly Kris Kringle as its department-store Santa, but Kris insists that he really is Santa Claus and gradually wins over practical Doris Walker, her skeptical daughter Susan and lawyer Fred Gailey. When Kris is committed and his sanity becomes a courtroom issue, Fred defends him by turning the question of Santa Claus into a legal test, while the Post Office's delivery of thousands of letters addressed to Santa gives the judge a way to recognize Kris without deciding the impossible. Susan and Doris regain their faith, and Kris quietly guides the three toward the Cape Cod house Susan has wished for.

episodes.title: One Way Passage (1949-12-30)
episodes.episodeDescription: Escaped convict Dan Hardesty, being returned to San Quentin to face execution, meets terminally ill Joan Ames aboard a Pacific liner. Neither initially reveals the death sentence hanging over them, and they fall in love while trying to crowd a lifetime of happiness into the voyage and a day ashore in Honolulu. At San Francisco Joan discovers Dan is the prisoner, runs after him for one final goodbye and dies as he is taken toward the death house. On New Year's Eve in Acapulco, their doctor watches two cocktail glasses mysteriously break with their stems crossed in the X Dan and Joan used to mark their happiest moments, suggesting they have found each other after death.

episodes.title: Magic Town (1950-01-06)
episodes.episodeDescription: Public-opinion expert Rip Smith discovers that the small town of Grandview is a mathematical mirror of the entire United States: its population, politics, income, religion, and voting patterns match national averages almost perfectly. Facing failure in his polling business, Rip secretly moves in as an insurance man and uses Grandview as a shortcut for national surveys. He also falls for local newspaper editor Mary Peterman, who is fighting for civic improvements and initially believes Rip has joined the town in good faith. Once his secret is exposed, national publicity turns Grandviewâ€™s status into a commercial craze, and the townspeople begin selling their opinions as if they were infallible. Their first self-conscious poll is spectacularly wrong, the boom collapses, and the town is humiliated. Rip then asks one final question: what does the average American do after making a mistake? Grandview answers by rebuilding together, proving its value not as a magic oracle but as a community capable of correcting itself, while Rip and Mary reconcile.

episodes.title: Tomorrow Is Forever (1950-01-13)
episodes.episodeDescription: Lieutenant John MacDonald is horribly wounded and reported dead at the end of World War I. Believing his shattered body and face would only destroy the life of his young wife Elizabeth, he lets her think he died and builds a new identity as Austrian chemist Erik Kessler. Elizabeth, pregnant with Johnâ€™s child, eventually marries her kind employer Larry Hamilton and raises her son Drew in a loving home. More than twenty years later Kessler comes to work for Larry and quietly meets the son he never knew, just as another war is beginning. Elizabeth gradually recognizes John beneath the altered face and confronts him with their old memories, but he refuses to reclaim her, insisting that Larry is now her true husband and that the past must remain past. He brings Drew home after the boy tries to leave for Canada to enlist, then tells Elizabeth to let their son follow his conscience. Kessler dies the next morning, leaving Elizabeth to understand that his final act of love was to protect the life she built without him.

episodes.episodeDescription: Professional gambler Joe Adams takes over a gambling ship and agrees to use it for Dorothy Bryant's wartime relief fundraiser, initially seeing the charity as just another angle. episodes.title: It Had to Be You (1950-01-27)
episodes.episodeDescription: Wealthy young sculptor Vicki Stafford is preparing to marry the respectable Oliver Harrington when a dashing man named George suddenly steps out of her imagination and begins disrupting the match. George insists that he is only a figment created from Vickiâ€™s dreams and that his purpose is to keep her from marrying the wrong man. As Vicki falls in love with him, childhood photographs reveal the real source of the fantasy: George looks exactly like Johnny Blaine, the little boy Vicki adored years earlier. George understands that Vicki is not meant for a dream at all but for the real Johnny, and arranges one last interruption of the wedding by calling the fire department. Fireman Johnny Blaine arrives, Vicki recognizes him instantly, and George disappears with his mission complete as the two childhood sweethearts rediscover each other.

episodes.title: The Sea Wolf (1950-02-03)
episodes.episodeDescription: After a ferry disaster, writer Humphrey Van Weyden and a young woman named Ruth are rescued by the sealing schooner Ghost, commanded by the brutal and intellectually formidable Wolf Larsen. Larsen rules his crew through fear, mocks compassion and religion, and refuses to let his unwilling passengers leave, forcing Van Weyden to confront a philosophy built entirely on strength and survival. As the voyage worsens, Larsen begins suffering violent headaches and periods of blindness, while his abused crew grows mutinous. An attack by Larsenâ€™s brother leaves the Ghost sinking and the crew gone. Van Weyden gets Ruth away in a lifeboat, then returns for supplies and finds Larsen alone, blind, and waist-deep in rising water. Larsen tries to keep Van Weyden with him so he will not die alone, but cannot stop his escape. The sinking captain is left reciting scripture, finally receiving the one thing he had never asked of anyone before: company at the edge of death.

episodes.title: This Thing Called Love (1950-02-10)
episodes.episodeDescription: Business statistician Anne Collins returns from a whirlwind marriage in Rio convinced that romance should be managed scientifically. When her mining-engineer husband Tice comes home after three months away, Anne announces that they will test her new marriage theory with a four-month platonic trial, separate rooms and an intellectual rather than emotional relationship. Tice is appalled but plays along, while Anneâ€™s carefully organized experiment produces jealousy, misunderstandings and escalating schemes. Needing financing from family-minded Peruvian investor SeÃ±or de Estro, Tice falsely implies that Anne is expecting a baby, forcing both spouses deeper into comic deception. Their arguments make it increasingly obvious that neither statistics nor rules can contain their attraction. Anne finally abandons the experiment and rewrites her theory around the emotional reality of marriage, concluding that a wife sometimes needs to be kissed rather than analyzed.

episodes.title: Its in the Bag (1950-02-17)
episodes.episodeDescription: Flea-circus operator Fred Floogle learns that his murdered Uncle Trumbull supposedly left him $300,000 hidden in one of a set of chairs that were sold at auction. Fred and his family chase the chairs from owner to owner while criminals and the uncle's lawyer Jefferson T. Pike pursue the same prize. The final chair exposes Pike as the uncle's killer and preserves the evidence against him, but Fred's hoped-for cash fortune turns out to be something else entirely: Trumbull's $300,000 is tied up in a murder story he wrote called Its in the Bag.

episodes.title: The Paleface (1950-03-03)
episodes.episodeDescription: The governor sends Calamity Jane undercover to stop renegade Preston from smuggling rifles and dynamite to hostile Indians. To maintain her cover she joins a wagon train and marries timid dentist Painless Peter Potter, who believes he has suddenly become a legendary frontier gunfighter whenever Jane secretly shoots from behind him. Painless basks in his accidental reputation while Preston mistakes him for the government agent and targets him for death. Captured by the Indians, Painless finally learns that his new wife is really Calamity Jane and that all of his miraculous marksmanship was hers. The pair escape in Prestonâ€™s wagon, accidentally setting off the dynamite shipment and destroying the contraband before it reaches the Indians. With the mission complete, Jane admits she loves Painless, although another assignment immediately threatens their long-delayed honeymoon.

episodes.title: Portrait of Jenny (1950-03-10)
episodes.episodeDescription: Struggling artist Eben Adams meets the mysterious Jennie in Central Park and discovers that each time she reappears she has aged years while almost no time has passed for him. Loving her transforms his work, and her portrait becomes the painting that finally gives his art life. Eben learns that Jennie belongs to another time and died in a New England storm, then races to the lighthouse where her fate is repeating. He reaches her but cannot defeat the great wave that takes her again. Years later, after Eben's own death, the story closes with the suggestion that the two have finally crossed time to reunite.

episodes.title: Champion (1950-03-17)
episodes.episodeDescription: Midge Kelly is a poor, angry drifter who discovers that boxing may be his way out of a life in which he feels like a nobody. Trainer Tommy Haley sees talent in him and helps turn him into a contender, but success feeds Midgeâ€™s ambition faster than his character. He discards people when they no longer serve him, threatens former lover Grace, abandons loyal relationships and even refuses to leave training when his dying mother calls for him. By the time he reaches the championship, his brother Connie sees how thoroughly the fight business and Midgeâ€™s hunger for status have corrupted him. In a savage title defense against Johnny Dunne, Midge is beaten nearly senseless but refuses to let Tommy throw in the towel. He rallies, knocks Dunne out and hears the crowd finally cheering his name, only to collapse moments later and die. Connie bitterly gives the reporters the conventional line that Midge went out like a champion, even though the victory has cost him everything.

episodes.title: Chicago Deadline (1950-03-24)
episodes.episodeDescription: Chicago reporter Ed Adams finds a young woman named Rosita dead of tuberculosis in a cheap hotel room and becomes obsessed with the address book she leaves behind. Working backward through its names, Ed discovers that Rosita had crossed paths with gamblers, wealthy financier G. G. Temple, gangster Sully Wellman, Blackie Franchot, John Spangler and others whose lives were damaged by the same violent circle. Temple had once struck Rosita and, believing he had killed her, relied on Sully to dispose of the body. Rosita was actually alive, and Spangler hid her until his unwanted advances drove her away again. Sully later killed Blackie and Spangler, used the secret to terrorize Temple into suicide, and tries to make Ed his fourth victim when the reporter finally reconstructs the chain. Belle Dorsett shoots Sully before he can kill Ed. Wounded and hospitalized, Ed knows he has finally met Rositaâ€™s funeral deadline: her story will be printed, and a woman who died almost unnoticed will at least be understood.

episodes.title: The Dark Mirror (1950-03-31)
episodes.episodeDescription: Identical twins Ruth and Terry Collins frustrate a murder investigation because police cannot prove which sister was with Dr. Peralta when he was stabbed. Psychologist Dr. Scott studies the twins and discovers that gentle Ruth is innocent while Terry is a paranoid personality driven by jealousy and capable of murder. Terry tries to impersonate Ruth and eliminate the people closing in on her. Police finally trap her by faking Ruth's death, provoking Terry into revealing herself. Ruth survives, Terry is taken for psychiatric treatment, and Scott promises Ruth that they will wait for the day her sister can recover.

episodes.title: The Fighting O Flynn (1950-04-07)
episodes.episodeDescription: Irish soldier of fortune Oâ€™Flynn returns home in 1797 and becomes entangled in a conspiracy tied to Napoleonâ€™s planned intervention in Ireland. His path repeatedly crosses Lady Benedetta, whose distrust gradually gives way to admiration as Oâ€™Flynn uncovers evidence that Lord Sedgemouth is working with the French and preparing a signal that will allow Bonaparteâ€™s forces to land. Branded a traitor and nearly executed, Oâ€™Flynn survives long enough to reach the fortress where the signal is to be sent. He scales the walls, defeats Sedgemouth in a sword fight, and prevents the rocket from being fired, leaving the French fleet waiting offshore for a signal that never comes. At dawn he returns wounded but victorious, and Benedetta finally admits that she no longer intends to resist him.

episodes.title: It Happens Every Spring (1950-04-14)
episodes.episodeDescription: College chemistry professor Vernon Simpson accidentally creates a substance that makes baseballs behave impossibly around wooden bats. Keeping his discovery secret, he joins a major-league club under an assumed identity and becomes a sensational pitcher whose baffling delivery carries the team toward the pennant while his university colleagues and sweetheart wonder where he disappeared. When the chemical supply runs out, Vernon believes his career is finished, only to discover in the final game that he can still pitch well without it. He returns to the university with baseball earnings, his scientific future restored, and his romance intact.

episodes.title: A Kiss in the Dark (1950-04-21)
episodes.episodeDescription: Concert pianist Eric Phillips unexpectedly becomes owner of the Cleopatra Arms apartment house and initially sees its tenants and problems as annoyances distracting him from his career. Model Polly Haynes and devoted manager Willoughby gradually force him to see the people behind the property, especially after he learns Willoughby ruined himself financially trying to care for the building and its residents. Eric begins using his money and influence to solve their problems instead of escaping them, restores Willoughby as manager for life, and discovers that his growing concern for the tenants is inseparable from his love for Polly.

episodes.title: Rope of Sand (1950-04-28)
episodes.episodeDescription: Mike Davis returns to South Africa two years after being tortured by the diamond syndicate, determined to recover a cache of stones he hid in the forbidden desert. Syndicate men Martingale and Vogel use dancer Suzanne Renaud to win Mike's confidence and learn the location, but Suzanne falls in love with him and secretly tries to keep him alive. Mike gives her a map, then discovers it was passed to Vogel and believes she betrayed him. After surviving another attempt on his life, Mike recovers the diamonds. The final confrontation exposes Vogel as a killer and Martingale manipulates events so Vogel dies rather than share the fortune. Martingale then reveals Suzanne surrendered the map only to protect Mike, and Mike leaves Africa with both the diamonds and the woman he nearly misjudged.

episodes.displayTitle: When My Baby Smiles at Me (1950-05-05)
episodes.episodeDescription: Burlesque partners Skid Johnson and Bonnie Kane marry and build an act together, but Skid's Broadway success, drinking and involvement with dancer Sylvia Marco pull him away from Bonnie and eventually break up their partnership. Bonnie tries to move on while Skid's career and health collapse under alcohol, leaving him barely able to perform. When she finds him failing backstage, Bonnie returns to the act, holds him up through the number and reveals that she never married the wealthy rancher who courted her because she still loves Skid; the pair reunite onstage and off.

episodes.title: Butch Minds the Baby (1950-05-12)
episodes.episodeDescription: Paroled safecracker Big Butch is trying to stay straight when gangster Harry the Horse recruits him for one more job. Butch agrees only because widowed Susie O'Neill and her baby Michael desperately need money, and the robbery becomes farcical when he has to mind the baby at the same time. After the safe is blown, Butch tries to return a stolen check so its owner will avoid tax trouble and so Michael can win a promised baby-contest prize. His parole officer discovers the scheme, but recognizes that Butch's motive was to help Susie rather than enrich himself. Butch still expects to answer for the crime, yet walks away feeling that for once he has come out on top by doing something for someone else.

episodes.title: Miss Grant Takes Richmond (1950-05-19)
episodes.episodeDescription: Inexperienced secretary Ellen Grant is hired by Dick Richmond's real-estate office without realizing that the business is largely a respectable front for illegal bookmaking. Taking the company at face value, Ellen enthusiastically proposes an affordable housing development and is put in charge, forcing Richmond and his partners to turn their fake operation into a real construction project to protect their cover. Her chaotic management creates comic disasters, but the houses become genuine and worthwhile. Ellen's faith in Richmond pushes him away from the racket, and the scheme that began as camouflage ends by giving him a legitimate business and a romance with the secretary who accidentally reformed it.

episodes.title: Flamingo Road (1950-05-26)
episodes.episodeDescription: Carnival dancer Lane Bellamy leaves the road behind and tries to build a respectable life in a small Southern town, but political boss Sheriff Titus Semple decides she is unsuitable for deputy Fielding Carlisle and uses his power to drive them apart. Lane later marries businessman Dan Reynolds and enters the world of local politics, where Semple's machine keeps tightening its grip. As corruption and personal revenge collide, Semple comes to Lane's home armed and threatens her. She kills him in self-defense, the grand jury clears her, and the collapse of Semple's political machine gives Lane and Dan a chance to start over on Flamingo Road.

episodes.title: She Wouldnt Say Yes (1950-06-02)
episodes.episodeDescription: Psychiatrist Susan Lane meets irrepressible cartoonist Michael Kent, creator of the mischievous Nixie, and is immediately irritated by his determination to turn every encounter into a romance. Their feud follows them onto a train, through Susanâ€™s treatment of an emotionally troubled young woman, and into a string of schemes in which each tries to prove the other is the one behaving irrationally. Susan insists she is too disciplined and well balanced to fall in love, while Michael keeps forcing her to confront the feelings she is trying to diagnose away. When jealousy and a rival blonde finally push Susan past her professional defenses, she admits that she loves Michael and asks him to marry her. He briefly needles her by walking away, then returns with lilacs, and Susan happily accepts the emotional disorder she had spent the story trying to cure.

episodes.title: Mr Blandings Builds His Dream House (1950-06-09)
episodes.displayTitle: Mr Blandings Builds His Dream House (1950-06-09)
episodes.episodeDescription: New York advertising executive Jim Blandings and his wife Muriel flee their cramped apartment for what looks like an idyllic Connecticut farmhouse, only to learn that the old house must be torn down and their affordable country dream rebuilt from scratch. Construction costs explode through rock blasting, a vanishing water supply, an endlessly deep well and one expensive surprise after another until Jim's planned $10,000 home becomes a roughly $48,000 ordeal. At the same time he is under pressure to invent a new slogan for the Wham Ham account. Household worker Gussie casually supplies the winning line, saving Jim's job, and after all the grief, debt and jealousy, Jim admits that if he had to do it over again he would still build the dream house.

episodes.title: The Strange Love of Martha Ivers (1950-06-23)
episodes.displayTitle: The Strange Love of Martha Ivers (1950-06-23)
episodes.episodeDescription: As a child Martha Ivers kills her domineering aunt while Walter O'Neil witnesses the crime, and their later testimony helps send an innocent man to his death. Years afterward Martha controls Iverstown and is trapped in a bitter marriage to Walter when childhood friend Sam Masterson unexpectedly returns. Martha and Walter fear Sam knows their secret, but Sam reveals he left before the killing and never witnessed it. Martha tries to draw Sam back into her life and ultimately urges him to remove Walter, but he refuses to become part of their guilt and walks away. Left together with the truth and their hatred, Martha and Walter bring their destructive marriage to a fatal end.

episodes.title: Shadow of a Doubt (1950-11-09)
episodes.episodeDescription: Young Charlie Newton is thrilled when her adored Uncle Charlie visits the family in Santa Rosa, but clues from two investigators and a newspaper story make her realize he is the wanted 'Merry Widow Murderer.' She keeps silent to protect her mother while trying to force him to leave, and Uncle Charlie responds by attempting to kill her, including trapping her in a garage filling with exhaust. Their final struggle ends with Uncle Charlie dead, while the family believes his death was accidental. Charlie alone is left with the knowledge that the charming uncle she worshiped was a serial killer.

episodes.title: Lifeboat (1950-11-16)
episodes.episodeDescription: Survivors of a ship torpedoed in the Atlantic crowd into a lifeboat, joined by Willi, a German from the U-boat that sank them. The Americans and Britons argue over whether to trust him, but gradually surrender navigation and survival decisions to the calm, capable sailor. They discover too late that Willi has hidden water and supplies, deceived them about their course and is steering them toward a German vessel; after the injured Gus dies and Willi's betrayal becomes undeniable, the survivors turn on and kill him. Forced to row and think for themselves, they are finally spotted during a naval battle and expect rescue. When another young German sailor climbs aboard with a gun, they disarm rather than kill him, ending with the unresolved question of what war requires people to become.
